21.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht set up in 1998 by SNS REAAL, independent since that group's nationalisation in 2013.
21.money: Stichting Beheer SNS REAAL supplies its budget, €12 million in donations for 2026.
21.arts: It funds art, culture and education projects for young people aged 12 to 30.

aatoserkko.what: A private Finnish foundation set up in Helsinki in 2002 by the newspaper publisher Aatos Erkko and his wife Jane, mainly to fund research in technology, economics and medicine.
aatoserkko.money: Returns on Sanoma shares Aatos Erkko left it in 2012, worth about 700 million euros, which made it Sanoma's largest shareholder.
aatoserkko.arts: It also supports arts and culture, and gave grants of 45.2 million euros across all its fields in 2020.

abnamro.money: ABN AMRO's money comes from retail, private and corporate banking, mainly in the Netherlands; Neuflize OBC is its private bank in France.

facts.t: In April 2021 ABN AMRO paid 480 million euros, a 300 million euro fine and 180 million euros in disgorged gains, to settle a Dutch criminal case over serious shortcomings in money laundering prevention.
ABN AMRO Bank N.V. declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

accessbank.money: Access Bank’s money comes from banking in Nigeria and other African countries.

adani.money: The Adani Group’s money comes from ports, power, coal mining and trading, airports and renewable energy in India and abroad.

facts.t: The Adani portfolio reported record EBITDA of INR 89,806 crore (US$10.5 billion) for the year to March 2025, up 8.2%.
In January 2023 the short seller Hindenburg Research published a report accusing the Adani Group of a stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme over decades.

In November 2024 US prosecutors indicted Gautam Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani and five others; the SEC accused them of conspiring to pay about $265m in bribes to Indian officials for solar power contracts.

In May 2026 the US Justice Department moved to dismiss the criminal charges against Gautam Adani after he pledged a $10bn US investment; the Treasury announced a $275m settlement with Adani over alleged Iran sanctions violations.

Adani North America and its affiliates reported $110,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; two outside firms also reported $50,000 in fees from Adani Green Energy.

adelson.money: The Adelson family's money comes from Las Vegas Sands, the casino company Sheldon Adelson founded, which owns Marina Bay Sands in Singapore and resorts in Macao.

facts.t: Las Vegas Sands' revenue was $13,017 million in 2025.
In January 2017 Las Vegas Sands agreed to pay a $6.96 million criminal penalty to end a US Justice Department probe into payments to a consultant in China, under the federal anti-bribery law.
Outside firms reported $872,500 in 2025 fees from Las Vegas Sands Corporation for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; it filed no in-house report.

aes.money: AES’s money comes from generating and distributing electricity in the United States and abroad, Panama among its markets.

facts.t: AES reported total revenue of $12,233 million for 2025; net income attributable to the company fell 46% to $910 million.
The AES Corporation reported $560,000 in its own federal lobbying reports for 2025 ($420,000, $60,000, $40,000 and $40,000 by quarter).

aesop.what: An Australian cosmetics brand founded in 1987 by the hairdresser Dennis Paphitis in Armadale, Melbourne; headquartered in Collingwood, Victoria, and owned by L'Oréal since 2023.
aesop.money: Sales of its skincare, haircare and fragrance products, as a subsidiary of L'Oréal.

afac.what: An independent non-profit founded in 2007 by Arab cultural activists that gives grants to artists, writers, researchers and cultural groups across the Arab region; based in Beirut.
afac.money: Donations, mainly from businesspeople and organisations in the Arab region, plus individual Friends and partner foundations and companies.
afac.arts: From 2007 to 2021 it raised slightly more than US$47 million and gave almost US$36 million in grants.

africell.money: Africell’s money comes from mobile phone networks in Africa.

facts.t: An outside firm reported $330,000 in 2025 fees from Africell UK Limited for US federal lobbying, on funding for broader mobile coverage in Africa.

ag2rlamondiale.what: A French social protection and insurance group run jointly by employers and unions and as a mutual; La Mondiale was founded in 1905 by seven northern industrialists.
ag2rlamondiale.money: Supplementary pensions, provident and health insurance, life insurance and savings: revenue of €13.1 billion in 2025.

ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.what: The real estate subsidiary of A. Ahlström Oy, a Finnish family investment company; it owns and maintains Villa Mairea and runs the Ahlström Estate in Noormarkku.
ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.money: Its parent's investments in industry, real estate and forest; the companies A. Ahlström owns had about EUR 5.5 billion of revenue in 2025.

aircanada.money: Air Canada’s money comes from passenger and cargo flights.

facts.t: Air Canada reported operating revenues of $22.4 billion for 2025 and operating income of $918 million.

airnorth.money: Air North’s money comes from flying: it is an airline based in Whitehorse serving Yukon and the Northwest Territories.

ajuntamentdebarcelona.what: The municipal government of Barcelona, elected every four years since 1979 and led by mayor Jaume Collboni; seated in the Casa de la Ciutat.
ajuntamentdebarcelona.money: The city's municipal budget: 4,180 million euros for 2026.

akerbp.money: Aker BP’s money comes from oil and gas on the Norwegian continental shelf; Aker ASA, controlled by Kjell Inge Røkke, and BP are its largest owners.

ako.what: A London charitable foundation set up in 2013 by Nicolai Tangen, founder of the hedge fund AKO Capital, who left its board in 2020.
ako.money: Gifts from Nicolai Tangen, who in 2020 gave it substantially all of his partnership interest in AKO Capital and other investment assets.

alfagroup.money: The money comes from Alfa Group’s businesses, above all Alfa-Bank, Russia’s largest privately owned bank, built by Mikhail Fridman, Petr Aven and their partners.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury made Alfa-Bank, Russia’s largest privately owned financial institution, subject to its directive on new debt and equity.
On 6 April 2022 the US Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on Alfa-Bank and six subsidiaries.

aliph.what: A Geneva foundation set up in March 2017 at the initiative of France and the United Arab Emirates to protect heritage, with the immunities of an intergovernmental organisation.
aliph.money: Contributions from states including France, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Morocco, Luxembourg, China and Cyprus, plus the Mellon Foundation, the Getty and private donors.

allianz.money: Allianz's money comes from insurance (property-casualty and life and health) and asset management.

facts.t: Allianz reported a record operating profit of 17.4 billion euros for 2025 and shareholders' core net income of 11.1 billion euros.

In May 2022 Allianz agreed to pay more than $6 billion, and its US asset management unit to plead guilty to criminal securities fraud, over the collapse of its Structured Alpha funds early in the Covid-19 pandemic.
Allianz SE declared EU lobbying costs of €2,250,000 to €2,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
AZOA Services Corp (Allianz of America) and affiliates reported $2,040,000 of their own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

almada.money: Al Mada’s money comes from its holdings in financial services (Attijariwafa bank), telecommunications, construction materials, retail, mining, energy, real estate and tourism.

facts.t: Attijariwafa bank, the group’s bank, reported net income group share of 9.5 billion dirhams for 2024, up 26.6% from 7.5 billion in 2023.
Nareva, which the register entry calls a subsidiary of the Al Mada Group, declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2024, with 6 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

alserkal.money: The Alserkal family’s Alserkal Avenue, founded by Abdelmonem Bin Eisa Alserkal, is an industrial compound of warehouses in Al Quoz, Dubai, that it leases to galleries and businesses.

americanexpress.money: American Express's money comes from card fees, interest on card lending and the charges merchants pay on card spending.

facts.t: American Express's revenue was $66,973 million in 2025.
American Express Company reported $1,680,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
American Express Corporation declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

ammodo.what: A Dutch foundation set up in Amsterdam in 2011 that funds visual and performing arts, science and architecture.
ammodo.money: Mainly donations from the Inphykem Foundation, former sole owner of the pension insurer Optas, which it sold to Aegon in 2007.
ammodo.arts: Ammodo Art supports new visual and performing arts productions and development programmes with partner institutions.

amorepacific.money: Amorepacific’s money comes from cosmetics and personal care, sold under brands such as Sulwhasoo, Laneige and Innisfree.

facts.t: Amorepacific Co., the group’s flagship company, reported 2025 sales of 4.2528 trillion won and operating profit of 335.8 billion won.
The Korea Fair Trade Commission fined Amorepacific 500 million won for abusing its power over door-to-door sales agencies by moving about 3,480 of their sales agents between 2005 and June 2013.

ampersand.what: A UK grant-making charity for the visual arts founded in 2011 by the collector Jack Kirkland, a director and shareholder of the Bowmer + Kirkland group.
ampersand.money: Donations from founder Jack Kirkland, including £319,744 in 2024-25 from his 2003 family settlement, plus investment income.
ampersand.arts: Its biennial Ampersand Foundation Award gives a Plus Tate member institution the funds for its director's or curator's chosen project.

ampol.money: Ampol, formerly Caltex Australia, refines and sells transport fuels, with the Lytton refinery and a national chain of service stations.

facts.t: Ampol reported RCOP net profit after tax of $429 million and statutory net profit of $82.4 million for 2025.
In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Ampol Limited disclosed $109,000 in political donations: $66,000 to Labor branches and $43,000 to Liberal and National branches.

amsterdamsvoordekunst.what: Amsterdam's arts fund, set up in 1972 to award the city's arts commissions and prizes, managing part of the municipal arts subsidy independently.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.money: The Municipality of Amsterdam, which funds it to carry out the city's Kunstenplan arts policy.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.arts: It runs multi-year subsidies under the Kunstenplan 2025-2028, one-off project grants and the Amsterdam Prize for the Arts.

andywarhol.money: The Andy Warhol Foundation's money comes from Andy Warhol's estate: its endowment and the licensing and sale of his work.

facts.t: Its Form 990-PF for the year to April 2025 shows revenue of $24,321,526, expenses of $27,558,476 and net assets of $387,156,946.

In May 2023 the US Supreme Court held that the foundation's commercial licensing of Warhol's Orange Prince to Condé Nast, based on Lynn Goldsmith's photograph, did not favour a fair use defence to copyright infringement, affirming the appeals court.

andywarholforvisualarts.what: A New York foundation set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which acts as the artist's estate and makes grants to the visual arts.
andywarholforvisualarts.money: An endowment built from Warhol's estate, sales of his works through Christie's and fees for licensing his images.
andywarholforvisualarts.arts: It has given over $300 million in cash grants to more than 1,000 arts organisations and donated 52,786 works to 322 institutions.

angelramos.money: The Fundación Ángel Ramos carries the name of Ángel Ramos, the Puerto Rican owner of the newspaper El Mundo and founder of the island’s Telemundo station.

angloamerican.money: Anglo American’s money comes from mining, mainly copper and iron ore, and, through De Beers, diamonds.

facts.t: For 2025 Anglo American reported underlying EBITDA of $6.4 billion and a loss attributable to shareholders of $3.7 billion, including a $2.3 billion impairment on De Beers.

A class action for 140,000 women and children in Kabwe, Zambia, alleges lead poisoning from a mine Anglo American ran from 1925 to 1974; the Johannesburg High Court refused to certify it in December 2023 and allowed an appeal in April 2024.
Anglo American reported $180,000 in its own 2025 US federal lobbying reports, on mining and critical minerals, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
De Beers plc reported $260,000 in its own 2025 US federal lobbying reports (its second-quarter report gives no amount), on US tariffs on natural diamonds.

annenberg.money: The Annenberg money comes from Walter Annenberg's Triangle Publications, publisher of The Philadelphia Inquirer, TV Guide, the Daily Racing Form and Seventeen, which he sold to Rupert Murdoch in 1988.

facts.t: The Annenberg Foundation reported total assets of $1,462,008,226 at the end of 2023 and paid $200,588,922 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).

ansamcal.money: ANSA McAL’s money comes from a Trinidad and Tobago conglomerate of manufacturing, beverages, retail and distribution, and financial services.

facts.t: ANSA McAL’s revenue grew 9% to TT$7.788 billion in 2025 and its profit before tax rose 10% to TT$1.014 billion.

anschutz.what: A private foundation in Denver, tax-exempt since 1984, through which the billionaire Philip Anschutz makes grants.
anschutz.money: Dividends and asset sales on net assets of US$1.65 billion (fiscal 2024); Anschutz's fortune comes from oil, railroads and entertainment.

anthonyharper.money: A New Zealand law firm; its money is its partners' fees from legal work.

anz.money: ANZ is one of Australia’s four major banks.

facts.t: In December 2025 the Federal Court ordered ANZ to pay $250 million in penalties for misconduct and systemic risk failures, including its handling of a $14 billion government bond deal and harm to at least 65,000 retail customers.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, ANZ Banking Group Limited disclosed $115,000 in political donations: $50,000 to Labor branches and $65,000 to Liberal and National branches.

apeejay.money: The Paul family's money comes from the Apeejay Surrendra Group, a Kolkata conglomerate in hotels (The Park), tea, shipping and the Oxford Bookstore.

facts.t: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels, which owns the Park hotel chain, declared FY25 revenue from operations of ₹631.45 crore and a consolidated net profit of ₹83.6 crore.

apple.money: Apple's money comes from selling the iPhone and other devices, and from services such as the App Store.

facts.t: Apple's revenue was $416,161 million in its fiscal year to September 2025.
In March 2024 the European Commission fined Apple over €1.8 billion for abusing its dominant position in the distribution of music streaming apps through its App Store.
Apple Inc. reported $10,410,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Apple Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €8,000,000 to €8,999,999 for its year from October 2024 to September 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

aramco.money: Aramco’s money comes from producing and selling Saudi crude oil and gas and refined and chemical products; the Saudi state owns most of it.

facts.t: Aramco reported net income of $106.2 billion for 2024, down 12.4% from $121.3 billion in 2023.
In the Carbon Majors data for 2024, Saudi Aramco was the biggest state-controlled polluter, responsible for 1.7 billion tonnes of CO2, much of it from exported oil.
InfluenceMap gives Saudi Aramco a D- grade for its climate policy engagement.
The Brussels consultancy Boldt declared Aramco Overseas Company BV as a 2025 client on the European Green Deal and energy policy, for €25,000 to €49,999.

aranya.money: Aranya develops and runs a seaside resort and residential community at Beidaihe, Hebei, where UCCA Dune stands.

arpels.what: A Paris jewellery house founded in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, now part of the Swiss luxury group Richemont.
arpels.money: Jewellery and watch sales for its owner Richemont, the luxury holding company Johann Rupert founded in 1988.
arpels.arts: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, launched in 2020, supports the creation and promotion of dance works and dance education.

art.what: An independent UK membership charity organised in 1903 by the activist Christiana Herringham to help public museums acquire art; based in London.
art.money: Subscriptions from its 142,000 members, who buy the National Art Pass, plus trusts, foundations and donors; it takes no government or National Lottery money.
art.arts: Since 1903 it has helped bring over 860,000 works of art into UK public collections.

artbridges.what: A US nonprofit founded in 2017 by Alice Walton that funds exhibitions, collection loans and programmes of American art with more than 400 partner museums.
artbridges.money: Alice Walton's philanthropy: she founded it and leads its board, and she is heiress to the Walmart fortune of her father Sam Walton.

artjameel.what: An independent arts organisation set up in 2003 as part of Community Jameel, the philanthropy of the Saudi Jameel family, with centres in Jeddah and Dubai.
artjameel.money: The Jameel family, owners of Abdul Latif Jameel, a Jeddah group founded in 1945 that has distributed Toyota cars in Saudi Arabia since 1955.
artjameel.arts: It partnered with the Victoria and Albert Museum in London in 2003.

artscouncilengland|UK.what: England's national development agency for the arts, museums and libraries, set up by Royal Charter in 1994 as an arm's length body of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport.
artscouncilengland|UK.money: UK government grant-in-aid through the culture department and National Lottery proceeds: £578,077,000 and £250,259,000 respectively in 2024-25.
artscouncilengland|UK.arts: It took over the Museums, Libraries and Archives Council in 2011 and has distributed lottery money to the arts since 1994.

artscouncilni|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilni|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.

artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.

artscouncil|Ireland.what: Ireland's national government agency for funding, developing and promoting the arts, established in 1951.
artscouncil|Ireland.money: The Irish state, which channels its arts funding to artists and arts organisations through the council.

artsqueensland.what: The arts agency of the Queensland Government, a service area of the state Department of Education, based in Brisbane.
artsqueensland.money: The Queensland state budget: the arts portfolio received A$420.7 million for the first year of the Time to Shine strategy (2025).

asahi.money: The Asahi Shimbun’s money comes from newspaper publishing, digital media and property.

aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.what: The unitary local and regional government of the Auckland Region, formed in 2010 by merging seven territorial authorities and one regional council.
aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.money: The council group reported NZ$8.7 billion in revenue in 2025/26, which also funds its council-controlled organisations.

audain.money: Michael Audain’s money comes from Polygon Homes, the Vancouver home builder he chairs and is a major shareholder of; Polygon Homes also gives in its own name.

augustinusfonden.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1942 by Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker at the initiative of tobacco manufacturer Ludvig Augustinus; based in Copenhagen.
augustinusfonden.money: Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker, its wholly owned investment company, which grew from a 1750 tobacco mill and still holds about 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
augustinusfonden.arts: In 2021 it gave DKK 399 million, of which DKK 284 million went to art and culture.

axa.money: AXA's money comes from insurance and asset management.

facts.t: AXA declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

ayalapresentsshows.money: Ayala Corporation’s money comes from banking (BPI), property (Ayala Land), telecoms (Globe), energy (ACEN) and other units in the Philippines.

facts.t: Ayala Corporation’s core net income rose 7% to a record P48.3 billion in 2025, driven by Bank of the Philippine Islands and Ayala Land.

azurapower.money: Azura Power West Africa’s money comes from power generation in Nigeria.

b3.money: B3’s money comes from running Brazil’s stock exchange and its trading, clearing and registry services.

facts.t: B3’s recurring net profit was R$5.3 billion in 2025, up 10%.

baesystems.money: BAE Systems' money comes from making and selling weapons and military systems: combat aircraft, warships, submarines, armoured vehicles and munitions.

facts.t: BAE Systems reported record 2025 sales of £30.7bn, up 10%.

In March 2010 BAE Systems pleaded guilty in US District Court in Washington and was sentenced to pay a $400 million criminal fine for conspiring to defraud the United States, including false statements to US government agencies.

BAE Systems declared EU lobbying costs of €200,000 to €299,999 for its financial year November 2025 to October 2026 to the EU Transparency Register (register export of 16 November 2026; its LobbyFacts datacard still shows 2022).
BAE Systems, Inc. reported $4,240,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

bago.money: Laboratorios Bagó’s money comes from making and selling medicines; it is an Argentine pharmaceutical group.

bailletlatour.what: A Belgian foundation created by Alfred de Baillet Latour (1901 to 1980), the last male heir of his family, that funds health, education, culture, environment and Olympic sport.
bailletlatour.money: Its holding in the brewer AB InBev: 5,485,415 shares (0.27 percent) in 2019, held through the Stichting Fonds InBev Baillet Latour.
bailletlatour.arts: Since 2000 it has paid for the safeguarding, restoration and display of historic sites and artworks in Belgium.

bailliegifford.money: Baillie Gifford’s money comes from fees for managing investments in listed and private companies for clients.

facts.t: Baillie Gifford had £224 billion in assets under management and 1,738 staff in 2024.
Baillie Gifford said in 2024 that 2% of its clients’ money was invested in companies with some business related to fossil fuels.
In June 2024 Baillie Gifford ended all its remaining literary festival sponsorships, approximately £1M per year in funding.
Baillie Gifford declared EU lobbying costs under €10,000 for May 2025 to April 2026, with 0.5 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

bajaj.money: The Bajaj family's money comes from the Bajaj group's companies, among them the motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto and the lender Bajaj Finance.

facts.t: Bajaj Auto reported total operating income of Rs50,010 crore and profit after tax of Rs8,151 crore for FY2025.

In November 2023 the Reserve Bank of India stopped Bajaj Finance lending through its eCOM and Insta EMI Card products, citing key fact statements not given to borrowers; it lifted the restrictions on 2 May 2024 after remedial action.

balnaves.money: The Balnaves Foundation was set up in 2006 by Neil Balnaves, whose television production companies brought Big Brother and Bananas in Pyjamas to Australian screens.

bancatransilvania.what: Romania's largest bank, founded in Cluj-Napoca on 16 February 1993 by 46 local entrepreneurs with US$2 million of capital.
bancatransilvania.money: Retail, corporate and investment banking; it held about 23% of Romanian banking assets in 2026 and has no majority shareholder.

bancolombia.money: Bancolombia’s money comes from banking, mainly in Colombia.

facts.t: Grupo Bancolombia reported a consolidated profit of COP 6.3 trillion (6,3 billones) for 2024, the largest among Colombia’s lenders.

bancopopular.money: Popular, Inc.’s money comes from banking in Puerto Rico and the United States, through Banco Popular.

bankofamerica.money: Bank of America’s money comes from consumer and commercial banking, lending, wealth management and investment banking.

facts.t: Bank of America declared EU lobbying costs of €1,000,000 to €1,249,999 for 2025, with 3 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Bank of America a C- grade for its climate finance policy engagement.
Bank of America reported $2,850,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Bank of America’s federal PAC gave $488,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 59% to Republicans and 40% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

bankofchina.money: Bank of China is a state-owned commercial bank, one of China's largest lenders.

facts.t: Bank of China (Europe)'s Brussels branch declared EU lobbying costs of €10,000 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

bankwindhoek.money: Bank Windhoek’s money comes from banking in Namibia; it belongs to Capricorn Group.

banquenationale.what: Canada's sixth-largest commercial bank, created by an act of 4 May 1859 and headquartered in Montreal; it is the largest bank in Quebec.
banquenationale.money: Personal and commercial banking and wealth management, with 59% of revenue from Quebec in fiscal 2017.

barclays.money: Barclays' money comes from banking: UK retail and business banking, cards, and corporate and investment banking.

facts.t: Barclays reported profit before tax of £9.1 billion for 2025, up from £8.1 billion in 2024.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 names Barclays the largest British fossil fuel financier in 2025, with $34 billion, and the only European bank in its Dirty Dozen.
Barclays PLC declared EU lobbying costs of €1,000,000 to €1,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Barclays US GPF Inc. reported $850,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

barrick.money: Barrick’s money comes from gold and copper mining in North America, Africa, Latin America and Papua New Guinea.

facts.t: In February 2015 Acacia Mining, formerly African Barrick Gold, settled out of court with villagers over the deaths of six people at its North Mara mine in Tanzania.

Barrick Mining Corporation reported $1,900,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in three quarterly reports, and Barrick Gold of North America $1,290,000 in four, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

basellandschaft.what: A Swiss canton, traditionally the half-canton paired with Basel-Stadt, its urban counterpart, with its capital at Liestal.
basellandschaft.arts: Under the culture agreement its parliament approved in January 2020, it pays Basel-Stadt 9.6 million Swiss francs a year from 2022.

baselstadt|Switzerland.what: The Swiss canton made up of Basel, Riehen and Bettingen, the smallest canton by area.
baselstadt|Switzerland.money: The cantonal budget, from which its culture department pays four-year operating grants to institutions, with an annual contribution from Basel-Landschaft.

bayer.money: Bayer's money comes from crop science (seeds and pesticides, including Monsanto's glyphosate weedkiller Roundup), pharmaceuticals and consumer health products.

facts.t: Bayer reported 2024 group sales of 46.606 billion euros and net income of minus 2.552 billion euros.

In June 2020 Bayer said it would pay up to $10.9 billion to settle litigation over Monsanto's weedkiller Roundup, covering about 125,000 filed and unfiled claims: $8.8 billion to $9.6 billion for current litigation and $1.25 billion for potential future litigation, while maintaining that Roundup is safe.
Bayer AG declared EU lobbying costs of €6,000,000 to €6,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 20 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Bayer Corporation reported $9,190,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four consolidated quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

bbva.money: BBVA's money comes from retail and corporate banking, chiefly in Spain, Mexico, Turkey (through Garanti BBVA) and South America.

facts.t: The BBVA Group reported a result of €10,511m for 2025, up 4.5% on the year before.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks BBVA 31st among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, up $2.0 billion (23.1%) on 2024.
BBVA declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

bcartscouncil|Canada.what: An agency of the Province of British Columbia created in 1995 under the Arts Council Act; based in Victoria.
bcartscouncil|Canada.money: The British Columbia provincial budget, through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport.
bcartscouncil|Canada.arts: In the year to 31 March 2018 it gave over C$24 million in awards, grants and scholarships in 225 communities.

belfastcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for Belfast, Northern Ireland's largest city, with 60 councillors who meet at Belfast City Hall.
belfastcitycouncil|UK.money: The district rate on Belfast homes and businesses, which councillors set each year, raised by 4.48 per cent for 2026/27.
belfastcitycouncil|UK.arts: Its Community Festivals Fund gives local groups grants of £2,500 to £10,000 for community festivals.

belgiorno.money: The Belgiorno-Nettis family’s money comes from Transfield, the construction and engineering company Franco Belgiorno-Nettis set up with Carlo Salteri in 1956; the family owns Transfield Holdings and founded Transfield Services.

facts.t: Transfield Services, founded by the Belgiorno-Nettis family, managed Australia’s offshore mandatory detention centres for asylum seekers in 2014, when the Biennale of Sydney cut ties with Transfield, its controversial sponsor.

Ten years after the Biennale said it had cut all ties with Transfield, its 2024 report applauds 51 years of patronage by Transfield Holdings and the Belgiorno-Nettis family and lists both among its benefactors.

bellcanada.money: BCE’s money comes from Bell Canada’s wireless, internet and phone services and Bell Media.

benesse.money: Benesse’s money comes from education and publishing (correspondence courses, Berlitz language schools) and elderly care; the Fukutake family’s foundations hold its shares.

facts.t: In July 2014 Benesse disclosed a leak of customer records it later put at 35.04 million, and set aside 20 billion yen for compensation.

berlinsenate|Germany.what: The executive of the city-state of Berlin, made up of the Governing Mayor and up to ten senators, meeting weekly at the Rotes Rathaus.
berlinsenate|Germany.money: The Berlin state budget, adopted as a two-year budget, now for 2026 and 2027.

creditagricole.money: Crédit Agricole's money comes from banking, insurance and asset management; it is a French cooperative group of regional banks.

facts.t: Crédit Agricole Group reported 2025 revenues of €39,558 million and net income Group share of €8,754 million.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Crédit Agricole 30th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of -$1.0 billion (-8.4%) from 2024.
Crédit Agricole S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 2.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

crownfamily.money: The Crown family's money comes from Henry Crown and Company, its private investment firm, and from its stake in General Dynamics, the defence contractor into which Henry Crown's Material Service Corporation merged in 1959.

facts.t: General Dynamics, in which the Crown family is a major shareholder, reported 2025 revenue of $52.6 billion and net earnings of $4.2 billion.

crownresorts.money: Crown Resorts runs casinos in Melbourne, Perth and Sydney.

facts.t: In February 2021 the Bergin inquiry found Crown unfit to run its Sydney casino, finding that Crown subsidiaries were used to launder money and that the company’s conduct facilitated money laundering for at least five years.
In July 2023 the Federal Court ordered Crown Melbourne and Crown Perth to pay a combined civil penalty of $450 million for contraventions of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing law.

ctbc.money: CTBC's money comes from banking and insurance, through CTBC Financial Holding and its subsidiary CTBC Bank.

facts.t: In September 2018 the Taiwan High Court, at a retrial in the Red Fire case, found Jeffrey Koo Jr., chair of the Chinatrust charity foundation, guilty of violating the Financial Holding Company Act and cut his sentence from nine years and eight months to three years and six months; the case grew from CTBC Financial Holding's bid for a stake in Mega Financial Holding.

In April 2021 the High Court acquitted Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chair of Chinatrust Financial Holding, in the case over the 2006 sale of structured notes tied to Mega Financial Holding, after first and second rulings of nine years and of nine years and eight months; prosecutors could appeal.
In May 2025 the Taipei District Court sentenced Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chairman of CTBC Financial Holding, to seven years and eight months for his role in a building purchase scandal.

Prosecutors alleged that Jeffrey Koo Jr. and three former CTBC executives inflated the value of the Chengcing Lake Building by NT$100 million, causing losses to CTBC Bank; in May 2025 the court put them under daily monitoring as flight risks.
CTBC Financial Holding reported a consolidated after-tax net profit of NT$80.619 billion for 2025, a record, with earnings per share of NT$4.08.

By May 2026 the Red Fire case against Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chair of CTBC Financial Holding, had run for 20 years: he was acquitted at the second and at the third retrial, the Supreme Court overturned the third acquittal too, and the High Court opened a fourth retrial.

cuervo.money: The Beckmann family’s money comes from Becle, the maker of José Cuervo tequila and other spirits.

facts.t: Becle’s net sales were 43,087 million pesos in 2025, against 43,962 million in 2024 (Análisis B×+ results table).

cultuurfonds.what: A Dutch private foundation set up by Prince Bernhard in London in 1940, renamed in 2023 to drop his name, with its office in Amsterdam.
cultuurfonds.money: Proceeds from the VriendenLoterij and the Nederlandse Loterij, plus gifts and bequests from donors.
cultuurfonds.arts: It puts more than EUR 50 million a year into culture and nature.

dell.money: Michael Dell's money comes from Dell Technologies, the computer and data-centre maker he founded and runs.

facts.t: Forbes put Michael Dell's net worth at $197.7 billion on 17 November 2026.
Dell Technologies reported $5,640,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

delta.money: Delta Air Lines' money comes from flying passengers and cargo.

facts.t: Delta Air Lines reported full-year 2025 GAAP operating revenue of $63.4 billion.
Delta Air Lines reported $5,970,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

desjardins.money: Desjardins Group is a financial cooperative; its money comes from members’ banking, insurance and wealth management, mainly in Quebec and Ontario.

facts.t: Desjardins Group reported surplus earnings before member dividends of $3,811 million for 2025.

In June 2022 the Superior Court of Quebec approved a settlement of nearly $200.9 million in a class action over a data breach that compromised the data of 4.2 million people with active Desjardins accounts.

deutschebank.money: Deutsche Bank's money comes from corporate and investment banking, private and retail banking and asset management.

facts.t: Deutsche Bank reported 2025 profit before tax of 9.7 billion euros and net profit of 7.1 billion euros, double the year before.

In July 2020 New York's Department of Financial Services imposed a $150 million penalty on Deutsche Bank for compliance failures in its relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and its correspondent relationships with Danske Estonia and FBME Bank.
In January 2017 New York's Department of Financial Services fined Deutsche Bank $425 million for a Russian mirror-trading scheme it allowed its traders to run.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Deutsche Bank 20th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, up $2.9 billion (19.9%) on 2024.
Deutsche Bank AG declared EU lobbying costs of €1,500,000 to €1,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

deutschedenkmalschutz.what: A privately funded foundation set up on 17 April 1985, the largest private initiative for monument preservation in Germany, with its seat in Bonn.
deutschedenkmalschutz.money: Gifts from about 200,000 private donors and money from the GlücksSpirale lottery.
deutschedenkmalschutz.arts: It has helped preserve more than 7,400 monuments with almost 800 million euros in funding.

digicel.money: Digicel’s money comes from mobile and broadband services in the Caribbean and Central America; it was founded by Denis O’Brien.

facts.t: Bondholders took control of Digicel in a restructuring completed in January 2024 that cut Denis O’Brien’s stake to 10%.
With the 2023 restructuring of Digicel Group Holdings, the schemes cut the group’s consolidated debt by about $1.7 billion and its annual cash interest by about $120 million.
Digicel Holdings (Bermuda) paid the firm Checkmate Government Relations $420,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, as the firm reported.

disney.money: Disney's money comes from The Walt Disney Company's film, television, streaming and theme parks; some ties here are gifts of Disney family foundations, which are separate from the company.

facts.t: The Walt Disney Company reported revenues of $94.4 billion for fiscal 2025.
In September 2025 Disney agreed to pay $10 million to settle a lawsuit brought on the FTC's referral over collecting children's data from its YouTube videos.
Disney Worldwide Services, the company's lobbying arm, reported $4,550,000 of in-house US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

dnb.money: DNB's money comes from banking, mainly in Norway; Sparebankstiftelsen DNB, the savings bank foundation that gives most of the atlas ties here, owns DNB shares and gives from their dividends.

facts.t: DNB Group had a pre-tax operating profit of NOK 53.4 billion for 2025.
In May 2021 Finanstilsynet, Norway's financial supervisor, confirmed a NOK 400 million administrative fine on DNB for inadequate compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering Act.
DNB Bank ASA declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

doen.what: A Dutch foundation set up in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij that funds pioneers in the Netherlands and abroad.
doen.money: Lottery proceeds: 24,303,520 euros from the Postcode Loterij and 7,200,000 euros from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
doen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and culture projects in 2025.

dorotheum.what: An auction house founded in Vienna in 1707 by Emperor Joseph I; a state enterprise until its 2001 sale to Erwin and Hanno Soravia and Christoph Dichand.
dorotheum.money: Its auctions, retail sales and pawn lending; about 600 auctions a year bring some 60 percent of its turnover.

dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.what: The departmental government of Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France, run by an elected departmental council presided over by Martine Vassal, seated in Marseille.
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.money: The departmental budget its councillors adopted on 14 April 2026, with more than 1.6 billion euros, over 62 percent of spending, for social welfare.

droomendaad.what: A family foundation set up in Rotterdam on 13 December 2016 by Martijn van der Vorm, former chief executive of the investment company HAL; Van der Vorms chair its board.
droomendaad.money: The Van der Vorm family fortune, invested in HAL since the family sold its Holland America cruise business in 1988.
droomendaad.arts: It takes no applications and develops its own Rotterdam projects through foundations it sets up, among them the Fenix museum.

dubaiculture.what: A public authority of the Government of Dubai created by Law No. 6 of 2008, chaired since 5 September 2019 by Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.
dubaiculture.money: The general budget of the Emirate of Dubai, plus its own fees and grants or gifts approved by the Executive Council.

dublincitycouncil|Ireland.what: The local authority for the city of Dublin, called Dublin Corporation until 2001, with 63 elected members and a Lord Mayor.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.money: The council's own budget, from which its Arts Office pays annual arts grants and bursary awards.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.arts: It added €50,000 to its 2026 project grants and bursary awards.

dulux.money: Paint: in Australia and New Zealand Dulux belongs to DuluxGroup, owned by Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings; elsewhere the brand has been AkzoNobel's, and Nippon Paint agreed in 2026 to buy AkzoNobel's Dulux businesses in Southeast Asia.

facts.t: Nippon Paint Holdings' consolidated revenue rose 8.3% to ¥1,774,231 million in 2025, with operating profit of ¥257,104 million; DuluxGroup's revenue was ¥405,173 million.

In October 2026 Nippon Paint agreed to buy AkzoNobel's decorative paints businesses in Southeast Asia, Dulux their core brand, including the Indonesian joint venture, for an enterprise value of about $1.35 billion.

duvel.what: A Belgian family-owned brewer founded in 1871 by Jan-Leonard Moortgat, now in its fourth generation, based in Breendonk, Puurs-Sint-Amands.
duvel.money: Beer sales from brands including Duvel, Vedett, Chouffe and Liefmans: consolidated turnover of 608 million euros in 2024.

ecobank.money: Ecobank’s money comes from banking in 39 African countries.

facts.t: Ecobank’s net revenue rose 17% to $2.45 billion in 2025, and its pre-tax profit 21% to $801 million.

eczacibasi.money: The Eczacıbaşı family’s money comes from the Eczacıbaşı Group, a Turkish industrial group.

facts.t: The Eczacıbaşı Group reported net revenue of €1.9 billion for 2025, 53% of it from international operations.

egdholding.what: A Bergen family investment company founded in 1907 by Einar Galtung Døsvig. Its chairman, Espen Galtung Døsvig, represents the fourth generation.
egdholding.money: The family's holdings in shipping (eight ships through EGD Shipholding), property (EGD Property) and financial investments (EGD Capital).
egdholding.arts: Its registered purpose includes buying and selling art and building and lending out an art collection.

enabel.what: The Belgian federal government's agency for international cooperation, formerly the Belgian Technical Cooperation (CTB), with over 2,500 staff running over 200 projects.
enabel.money: Project work worth 500 million euros a year, at least half paid by the Belgian state, the rest by clients such as the European Union.

enbridge.money: Enbridge’s money comes from crude oil and gas pipelines across North America, gas utilities and some renewable power.

facts.t: Enbridge reported GAAP earnings attributable to common shareholders of $7,072 million for 2025, against $5,053 million in 2024.

In July 2016 Enbridge settled US claims over its 2010 oil spills in Marshall, Michigan and Romeoville, Illinois: $62 million in Clean Water Act penalties, $61 million of it for discharging at least 20,082 barrels of oil in Marshall, and at least $110 million in spill-prevention measures.
Enbridge (U.S.) reported $1,169,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

enel.money: Enel's money comes from generating, distributing and selling electricity and gas in Italy, Spain (Endesa) and Latin America; the Italian state is its largest shareholder.

facts.t: Enel reported 2025 revenues of 80,346 million euros and Group net ordinary income of 7,011 million euros.
InfluenceMap gives Enel a B- grade for its climate policy engagement (summary updated Q3 2026).
ENEL SpA declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 6 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

engie.money: Engie's money comes from selling gas and electricity, running power plants, renewables and gas networks, and energy services.

facts.t: ENGIE declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Engie North America reported $270,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Engie a C+ grade for its climate policy engagement.

eni.money: Eni’s money comes mainly from producing and selling oil and gas; the Italian state is a major shareholder.

facts.t: Eni reported adjusted net profit of €5,264 million for 2024, down 37% from €8,322 million in 2023.
Eni declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025, with 6.2 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Eni a D+ grade for its climate policy engagement.
Eni’s US operating company reported $40,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

eon.money: E.ON's money comes from running electricity and gas networks and selling energy to customers across Europe.

facts.t: In July 2009 the European Commission fined E.ON/E.ON Ruhrgas and GDF Suez €553 million each for agreeing not to sell gas carried over the MEGAL pipeline in each other's home markets.
InfluenceMap gives E.ON a C+ grade for its climate policy engagement (summary updated Q3 2026).
E.ON SE declared EU lobbying costs of €2,500,000 to €2,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 9.05 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

epson.money: Epson's money comes from making printers, projectors and other imaging equipment, through Seiko Epson of Japan.

facts.t: Seiko Epson reported revenue of ¥1,362,944 million and business profit of ¥89,589 million for the year ended 31 March 2025.

equinor.money: Equinor’s money comes mainly from oil and gas production, largely on the Norwegian shelf; the Norwegian state owns 67%.

facts.t: Equinor reported adjusted operating income of USD 29.8 billion and net income of USD 8.83 billion for 2024.
Equinor declared EU lobbying costs of €2,500,000 to €2,749,999 for 2025, with 6.8 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Equinor a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Equinor’s US operations reported $1,240,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

ericschmidt.money: Eric and Wendy Schmidt's money comes mostly from Google (Alphabet), which Eric Schmidt ran as chief executive and chairman.

erste.what: Austria's largest savings bank foundation, formed in 2003 from Erste österreichische Spar-Casse, the first Austrian savings bank (1819), seated in Vienna.
erste.money: Dividends from its stake as core shareholder of Erste Group Bank AG, part of which it spends on Central and South Eastern Europe.

erstebank.money: Erste Group's money comes from retail and commercial banking in Austria and Central and Eastern Europe; ERSTE Foundation, a savings bank foundation, is its main shareholder and funds culture from its dividends.

facts.t: Erste Group reported a net result of 3.5 billion euros for 2025, up from 3.1 billion euros in 2024.
Erste Group Bank AG declared EU lobbying costs of €300,000 to €399,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

esmefairbairn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity founded in 1961 by unit-trust pioneer Ian Fairbairn and named after his late second wife; based in London.
esmefairbairn.money: Investment returns on an endowment that began as a 33% stake in fund manager M&G, sold to Prudential in 1999.
esmefairbairn.arts: In 2025 it gave £52.9m across its three aims, one of which is Creative, Confident Communities.

espinosayglesias.money: Manuel Espinosa Yglesias made his money in cinemas and in banking, as the owner of Bancomer.

estrelladamm.what: A Barcelona brewery founded in 1876 by the Alsatians August Kuentzmann Damm and Joseph Damm, maker of Estrella Damm beer.
estrelladamm.money: Beer and drinks sales, EUR 2,061 million in 2023; in 2018 the Carceller family held the largest stake through Disa, a Canarian oil company.

esun.money: E.SUN's money comes from banking, through E.SUN Financial Holding and E.SUN Commercial Bank.

facts.t: E.SUN Financial Holding reported a 2025 after-tax net profit of NT$34.29 billion, up 31.2% and a record, on net revenue of NT$91.77 billion.

europeanregionaldevelopment.what: An EU fund set up in 1975 and one of the European Structural and Investment Funds, run by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy.
europeanregionaldevelopment.money: The EU budget, spent through programmes shared between the Commission and national and regional authorities, which choose the projects.

exxonmobil.money: ExxonMobil produces and refines oil and gas and makes chemicals; Mobil merged into it in 1999.

facts.t: ExxonMobil reported 2025 earnings of $28.8 billion and cash flow from operations of $52.0 billion.
In May 2022 Massachusetts' Supreme Judicial Court rejected ExxonMobil's bid to dismiss the state's 2019 lawsuit accusing it of misleading the public about climate change, so the case can go forward.
Exxon Mobil Corp reported $8,500,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
ExxonMobil Petroleum & Chemical declared EU lobbying costs of €4,000,000 to €4,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

fastretailing.money: Fast Retailing’s money comes from clothing retail, above all Uniqlo, and GU.

facts.t: Fast Retailing reported revenue of 3.4005 trillion yen for the year to August 2025, and operating profit of 564.2 billion yen.

US Customs and Border Protection blocked a January 2021 shipment of Uniqlo shirts under its order on cotton from the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, over forced-labour concerns, and rejected the company’s protest in May 2021.

federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.what: The German federal government's office for culture and media policy, headed by a Minister of State, currently Wolfram Weimer, with staff in Bonn and Berlin.
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.money: The federal budget: the cabinet set about €2.5 billion for culture and media in 2026.

ferrerangel.money: The Ferré-Rangel family’s money comes from El Nuevo Día, the Puerto Rican newspaper it owns.

fidelity.money: The Johnson family's money comes from Fidelity Investments, the Boston fund manager Edward C. Johnson II founded in 1946; the Fidelity Foundation is its US foundation and the Fidelity UK Foundation that of Fidelity International.

facts.t: Forbes says Fidelity Investments managed discretionary assets of $7.1 trillion as of December 2025, and that Abigail Johnson owns an estimated 29% of the firm.
FMR LLC, Fidelity's parent, reported $2,970,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

finnmarkcounty|Norway.what: The regional government of Finnmark county in northern Norway, re-established on 1 January 2024 after four years merged into Troms og Finnmark, with its administration in Vadsø.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.money: The county budget set by its elected county council.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.arts: It runs a culture and cultural heritage service and gives grants to festivals in the county.

flemishgovernment|Belgium.what: The executive of the Flemish Community and Flemish Region of Belgium, led by a Minister-President and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
flemishgovernment|Belgium.money: The Flemish public budget, which its Department of Culture, Youth and Media spends on arts subsidies under the Arts Decree (Kunstendecreet).

fletcher.money: Fletcher Building, a New Zealand building materials and construction group, came out of the Fletcher Challenge conglomerate that the Dunedin listing names.

facts.t: For the year to 30 June 2025 Fletcher Building reported revenue of $7 billion and a net loss of $419 million.
Fletcher Building set aside A$155 million (NZ$168 million) for a settlement over leaking pipes made by its Iplex subsidiary in Western Australian homes, without admitting liability.

florahewlett.what: A US private foundation in Menlo Park, California, set up in 1966 by Hewlett-Packard co-founder Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora.
florahewlett.money: An endowment of about US$13.9 billion at the end of 2024, from the Hewletts' personal gifts; it is independent of HP.
florahewlett.arts: Its Performing Arts programme awarded US$40.5 million in 94 grants in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2024.

fnbfirstrand.money: FirstRand’s money comes from banking, through FNB, RMB and WesBank; the Thapong tie is its Botswana arm’s FNB Foundation.

facts.t: FirstRand’s normalised earnings rose 10% to R41.8 billion in the year to June 2025.
In the same year it took a further R2.7 billion pre-tax provision tied to the UK investigation into the vehicle finance market, after R3 billion the year before.

fonalledas.money: The Fonalledas family’s money comes from Empresas Fonalledas, owner of the Plaza Las Américas shopping centre in San Juan.

fondazionecariplo.what: A foundation of banking origin created in Milan in December 1991, when the Amato law split the Cariplo savings bank into this foundation and a commercial bank.
fondazionecariplo.money: Returns on an endowment of 8,207,623,005 euros (2023) built on its stake in the Cariplo bank, which later merged into Intesa Sanpaolo.

fondazionecrfirenze.what: A Florence foundation of banking origin, created in April 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, a savings bank founded by 100 citizens in 1829, became a company.
fondazionecrfirenze.money: Returns on an endowment of about 2 billion euros inherited from the savings bank, including a holding in Intesa Sanpaolo.
fondazionecrfirenze.arts: Culture is one of its four missions, and its endowment includes an art collection.

fondazionecrt.what: A banking foundation formed in Turin in 1991, when the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino moved its banking business into a separate company; Italy's third-largest by assets.
fondazionecrt.money: Returns on its endowment, inherited from the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino and long including a large UniCredit shareholding.
fondazionecrt.arts: It has given more than 2 billion euros to over 50,000 projects in art, research, training, welfare, environment and innovation.

forartsinitiatives.what: A New York grant-making foundation that began in 1931 as the American Center for Students and Artists in Paris and took its present name in 2008.
forartsinitiatives.money: An endowment created from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture, now about $30 million.
forartsinitiatives.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and independent art spaces in many countries.

ford.money: The Ford Foundation was set up in 1936 by Edsel Ford, son of the Ford Motor Company's founder, with Ford money; it is independent of the company, and every tie in this ledger is the foundation's.

facts.t: The Ford Foundation reported total assets of $16,791,366,964 at the end of 2023 and $607,405,678 in grants paid that year, in its Form 990-PF.

fortabat.money: The Fortabat fortune came from the cement maker Loma Negra, which Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat sold in 2005.

facts.t: The sale of Loma Negra brought Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat US$1,025 million, from which US$440 million of debt had to be paid.

A 2014 study by Argentina’s Procuración General set out how Loma Negra gained from the 1976 coup and the 1977 murder of Carlos Alberto Moreno, a labour lawyer who had won occupational illness cases for its miners; Página/12 reported the inquiry moving to the board Amalia Fortabat chaired.

foundationnorth.money: An endowment that began with the ASB Bank shares settled on it under the Trustee Banks Restructuring Act 1988 (it was the ASB Community Trust); its grants are paid from the returns on its investment fund.

facts.t: In the year to 31 March 2026 Foundation North committed $72,018 thousand in grants and other funding, and held total assets of $1,951,081 thousand.

foyle.what: A UK grant-making charity formed in 2000 to carry out the will of bookseller Christina Foyle; it closed in December 2025 and entered voluntary liquidation in June 2026.
foyle.money: The estate of Christina Foyle, daughter of a founder of Foyles bookshop on Charing Cross Road, London.
foyle.arts: From 2000 to 2025 it gave over £185M to almost 7,500 charities and state schools, mainly for arts and learning.

frankenthaler.what: A New York non-profit formed by the painter Helen Frankenthaler in 1984; it became active in 2013, when her estate closed.
frankenthaler.money: Endowed by the artist; net assets were $173,182,625 in 2024, when sales of assets brought 86.3% of revenue.
frankenthaler.arts: Its Frankenthaler Climate Initiative made its first grants, totalling $5.1 million, in July 2021.

freelands.what: A London art education charity set up in 2015 by the media executive Elisabeth Murdoch, who chairs its board.
freelands.money: Investment income on a large 2019 donation, plus services donated by Freelands Group, owned by a trust of which Elisabeth Murdoch is a beneficiary.
freelands.arts: In 2025 it paid grants totalling £1,475,492 to 28 organisations.

frenchstate|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchstate|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

frittord.money: Fritt Ord was founded in 1974 by the Narvesen chain of convenience stores.

fukutake.what: A Japanese foundation that runs Benesse Art Site Naoshima with Benesse Corporation, grown from a foundation Soichiro Fukutake set up in 2004.
fukutake.money: A personal endowment from Soichiro Fukutake, former head of Benesse, the Okayama correspondence education and publishing company.
fukutake.arts: It has been a founding patron of CIMAM, the international committee for modern art museums, since 2000.

fundacilacaixa.what: A Spanish banking foundation that grew out of the la Caixa savings bank, headquartered in Barcelona since March 2025.
fundacilacaixa.money: Dividends from its holding company CriteriaCaixa, which holds 31 per cent of CaixaBank and 9.99 per cent of Telefónica.
fundacilacaixa.arts: Its social work budget, which covers cultural as well as social and scientific projects, is €710 million for 2026.

fundacinbbva.what: The foundation of the Spanish banking group BBVA, with headquarters in Bilbao and an office in Madrid.
fundacinbbva.money: The BBVA Group, whose corporate social responsibility the foundation carries out.

fundacincostantini.money: Eduardo Costantini’s money comes from Consultatio, his listed real estate company, known for the Nordelta gated communities.

facts.t: Costantini’s 72 percent stake in Consultatio was worth about US$580 million at the April 2024 share price.

fundacinjumexgrants.money: The López family’s money comes from Grupo Jumex, the Mexican juice and food company; Eugenio López Alonso is its heir.

facts.t: Expansión gave Jumex’s sales as between US$1,000 million and US$1,100 million, an analyst’s estimate, in 2013.

fundacinmutuamadrilea.what: The foundation of the Spanish insurer Mutua Madrileña, set up in 2003 for medical research and widened to social, road safety and cultural work in 2009.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.money: Funds from Mutua Madrileña, the Madrid insurer founded in 1930 that sells car, health and life insurance.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.arts: Cultural work takes about a quarter of the foundation's resources (2024).

gandel.money: The Gandel family’s money comes from shopping centres: John Gandel bought Melbourne’s Chadstone Shopping Centre in 1983, after growing his parents’ Sussan clothing chain with Marc Besen.

facts.t: In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, The Gandel Group Pty Ltd, the family company, disclosed $385,000 in political donations: $10,000 to Labor branches and $375,000 to Liberal and National branches.

garfieldweston.money: The Garfield Weston Foundation is a UK charity endowed by the Weston family; its income comes from Wittington Investments, of which it owns 79.2%, and through it a 46.0% holding in Associated British Foods (Primark, Twinings, British Sugar), whose controlling shareholder Wittington is. It is not the Canadian Weston branch (George Weston Ltd, Loblaw).

facts.t: Associated British Foods reported group revenue of £19,459m and adjusted operating profit of £1,734m for the 52 weeks to 13 September 2025.
At 5 April 2025 the Foundation owned 79.2% of Wittington Investments, the ultimate holding company of Associated British Foods, and through it 46.0% of ABF.

gates.money: Bill Gates's money comes from Microsoft, which he co-founded; the Gates Foundation is endowed from his fortune, and Microsoft's own gifts are named apart in these entries.

facts.t: The Gates Foundation reported total assets of $76,951,451,400 at the end of 2023 and paid $7,200,556,970 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).
Microsoft's revenue was $281,724 million in its fiscal year to June 2025.
Microsoft Corporation reported $9,360,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Microsoft Corporation declared EU lobbying costs of €7,000,000 to €7,999,999 for its year from July 2025 to June 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

gazprom.money: Gazprom’s money comes from natural gas: the state-controlled company is, in the US Treasury’s words, the world’s largest natural gas company, and it co-owns Belgazprombank in Belarus with Gazprombank.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury listed Gazprom, which it called the world’s largest natural gas company, among 11 entities owned or controlled by the Russian government that are subject to prohibitions on new debt and equity.

gazprombank.money: Gazprombank’s money comes from banking: Russia’s third-largest financial institution, closely tied to the energy sector, it co-owns Belgazprombank in Belarus with Gazprom.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury listed Gazprombank among 11 entities owned or controlled by the Russian government that are subject to prohibitions on new debt and equity.

On 21 November 2024 the US Treasury designated Gazprombank and six foreign subsidiaries, saying it is a conduit for Russia to buy military materiel and that the government uses it to pay soldiers, including combat bonuses.

geffen.money: David Geffen's money comes from the record labels he founded, Asylum, Geffen and DGC, and the film studio DreamWorks.

facts.t: Forbes put David Geffen's net worth at $9.7 billion on 17 November 2026.

generali.money: Generali's money comes from insurance and asset management; it is Italy's largest insurer.

facts.t: Generali reported a net result of €4,172 million for 2025, up 12.0% from €3,724 million in 2024.
Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 3.95 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

germanysforeignoffice.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanysforeignoffice.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

getty.money: The J. Paul Getty Trust is endowed by the oilman J. Paul Getty's bequest of Getty Oil stock; the J. Paul Getty Jr. Charitable Trust is the separate trust of his son, Sir Paul Getty.

facts.t: The J. Paul Getty Trust reported assets with a fair market value of $16,341,567,063 at the end of its tax year to June 2023, in its Form 990-PF.

gibbs.money: Alan Gibbs's fortune came from investment banking and deals such as the Freightways buyout, Telecom's privatisation and the founding of Sky TV, and later from Auckland's Viaduct Harbour land; Dame Jenny Gibbs is his former wife.

facts.t: Alan Gibbs gave $100,000 to the ACT Party in April 2008.
Alan Gibbs gave ACT another $100,000 the day before the 2008 election, disclosed under the Electoral Finance Act.

The Electoral Commission referred ACT to the police for disclosing late a series of donations, adding up to more than $30,000, from Alan Gibbs and Dame Jenny Gibbs, its biggest backers, made before the 2014 election.

godrej.money: The Godrej money comes from the Godrej companies; since the family's 2024 split, Jamshyd Godrej's side holds the unlisted Godrej & Boyce and its affiliates and a Mumbai land bank, and Adi and Nadir Godrej keep the listed Godrej Industries firms.

goetheinstitut.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goetheinstitut.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goldmansachs.money: Goldman Sachs is a US investment bank, trader and asset manager.

facts.t: Goldman Sachs reported 2025 net revenues of $58.28 billion and net earnings of $17.18 billion.

In October 2020 Goldman Sachs agreed to pay more than $2.9 billion to resolve US and other investigations into its role in the 1MDB scandal; the DOJ said it had conspired to use more than $1.6 billion in bribes to officials.
The Goldman Sachs Group reported $3,960,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
The Goldman Sachs Group declared EU lobbying costs of €1,500,000 to €1,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

goldsmith.what: A New York private foundation created in 1955 by Horace Ward Goldsmith, who bought a New York Stock Exchange seat in 1927.
goldsmith.money: Investment returns, chiefly gains on asset sales and dividends, on assets of $826 million in 2024.

google.money: Google's money comes from Alphabet, its parent, mainly from search and other advertising, with cloud services and YouTube.

facts.t: Alphabet's revenue was $402,836 million in 2025.
In September 2025 the European Commission fined Google €2.95 billion for abusing its dominance in online advertising technology.
Google Client Services LLC reported $13,100,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Google Ireland Limited and its affiliates declared EU lobbying costs of €5,500,000 to €5,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

gordondarling.money: The Gordon Darling Foundation was set up in June 1991 by the businessman Gordon Darling to support the visual arts through public institutions.

gracekennedy.money: GraceKennedy’s money comes from food manufacturing and distribution and from financial services, in Jamaica and abroad.

facts.t: GraceKennedy’s revenue rose 6.4% to J$177.8 billion in 2025, while net profit fell 18% to J$7.25 billion after Hurricane Melissa.

grupohabita.money: Grupo Habita’s money comes from running boutique hotels in Mexico.

grupoultra.money: Ultrapar’s money comes mainly from fuel distribution through Ipiranga, and from liquid bulk terminals (Ultracargo) and gas (Ultragaz).

facts.t: Ultrapar reported net profit of R$2.542 billion for 2025, up 1%, on net revenue of R$142.478 billion.

gucci.what: An Italian luxury fashion house founded in Florence in 1921 by Guccio Gucci and owned since 1999 by the French luxury group Kering.
gucci.money: Sales of clothing, leather goods, shoes and accessories: 7.65 billion euros in 2024.

gulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
gulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

hanwha.money: Hanwha’s money comes from a conglomerate of defence and aerospace, shipbuilding, chemicals, solar energy, finance and retail.

facts.t: Hanwha Aerospace, the group’s defence company, reported 2025 consolidated revenue of 26.7 trillion won and operating profit of 3.09 trillion won.
Norway’s sovereign wealth fund excluded Hanwha Corporation from 2008 for producing cluster munitions, and revoked the exclusion in 2021 after the company said it had stopped.

harphelu.money: Alfredo Harp Helú made his fortune in banking, as a main shareholder of Banamex.

hauser.what: A commercial art gallery founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.
hauser.money: Its gallery business: it represents over 80 artists and estates, including those of Philip Guston and Louise Bourgeois.

hdfc.money: HDFC's money comes from banking: HDFC Limited, the mortgage lender named at the museum, merged into HDFC Bank in 2023.

facts.t: HDFC Bank reported a net profit of ₹67,347.4 crore for FY 2024-25, up from ₹60,812.3 crore.

In September 2025 the Dubai Financial Services Authority banned HDFC Bank's Dubai branch from onboarding new clients, over its servicing of customers who had not been onboarded as clients of the branch.

hearst.money: Hearst's money comes from the privately held Hearst Corporation's magazines, newspapers, television stations and business information services; the Hearst Foundations are its family's charities.

facts.t: Outside firms reported $440,000 in 2025 fees for US federal lobbying from Hearst Corporation ($360,000) and Hearst Television ($80,000); Hearst filed no in-house report.

heinz.money: The Heinz Endowments' money comes from the Heinz family's fortune from the H. J. Heinz food company of Pittsburgh.

facts.t: The Heinz Endowments reported total assets of $2,130,567,687 at the end of 2023 and paid $48,689,957 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).

helis.what: A Louisiana private foundation established and funded in 1955 by the family of William Helis, a Greek emigrant to New Orleans who made a fortune in oil.
helis.money: The Helis family's oil fortune, plus art funds bequeathed by Diana Helis Henry and Adrienne Helis Malvin. Total assets were US$82,984,093 in 2024.
helis.arts: Its Art Funds paid for Prospect.3's Basquiat and the Bayou and for installing Lynda Benglis's The Wave of the World in New Orleans City Park.

henkel.money: Henkel's money comes from adhesives and from consumer brands in laundry, home and hair care.

facts.t: Henkel AG & Co. KGaA declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Henkel of America reported $607,000 of its own US federal lobbying for 2025 in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

henrymoore.what: A charity founded in 1977 by sculptor Henry Moore and his family, with headquarters at his former home in Perry Green, Hertfordshire, and the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds.
henrymoore.money: A founding gift from Henry Moore and his family; it also administers the sale and exhibition of Moore's work.
henrymoore.arts: Henry Moore Grants fund sculpture exhibitions, commissions, acquisitions and research, with grants of up to £20,000 in the main categories.

heritageexpeditions.money: Expedition cruises in Antarctica, the Subantarctic and the Pacific, run by the Russ family from Christchurch.

hermes.money: Hermès's money comes from selling luxury leather goods, silk, ready-to-wear and perfume; the Hermès family controls the company.

facts.t: Hermès reported 2025 revenue of €16,002 million and net profit (group share) of €4,524 million.
Hermès International declared EU lobbying costs of €50,000 to €99,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 0.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

hiridjee.money: The Hiridjee family’s money comes from Axian Group, a pan-African group in telecommunications, energy, real estate and financial services led by Hassanein Hiridjee.

hiscox.what: An insurance group listed on the London Stock Exchange and based in Hamilton, Bermuda, grown from a Lloyd's of London underwriting agency that began in 1901.
hiscox.money: Specialist insurance, including property, casualty, kidnap and ransom and hacking cover: revenue of £4,883.7 million in 2025.

hofffamily.money: The Hoffs’ money comes from Rolf Hoff’s business, which makes signage and produces artworks for artists.

hsbc.money: HSBC’s money comes from banking: lending, deposits, payments, wealth management and markets.

facts.t: HSBC Holdings reported a 2025 profit before tax of $29.9 billion, down $2.4 billion from 2024, on revenue of $68.3 billion.

In December 2012 HSBC Holdings and HSBC Bank USA admitted anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, forfeited $1.256 billion under a deferred prosecution agreement and agreed to $665 million in civil penalties; the US Attorney said its failures let at least $881 million in drug proceeds be laundered through the US financial system.

In October 2022 the UK Advertising Standards Authority upheld complaints against two HSBC UK climate posters and told the bank its environmental claims must not omit material information about its contribution to carbon dioxide and greenhouse gas emissions.
HSBC Holdings declared EU lobbying costs of €1,000,000 to €1,249,999 for the financial year February 2024 to January 2025, with 3 full-time-equivalent lobbyists and 78 high-level Commission meetings.

HSBC Technology and Services USA reported $1,080,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; outside firms also lobbied for HSBC units.

hugoboss.what: A German fashion company founded in 1924 by Hugo Ferdinand Boss in Metzingen, majority-owned since October 2026 by the British retailer Frasers Group.
hugoboss.money: Sales of BOSS and HUGO clothing, shoes and accessories: 4.27 billion euros in 2025.
hugoboss.arts: It has funded the HUGO BOSS PRIZE with the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation since 1996 and gave the HUGO BOSS ASIA ART Award from 2013.

hxexpeditions.money: Expedition cruise fares; since February 2025 HX has been owned by a consortium of investors led by Arini Capital Management, Cyrus Capital Partners and Tresidor Investment Management.

facts.t: HX calls itself the largest provider of expedition cruises to Antarctica, with five ships and just under 1,000 staff.
The investors who bought HX from Hurtigruten Group put in about EUR 140M of new junior funding.

hydroquebec.money: Hydro-Québec is the Quebec government’s electricity utility; its money comes from selling power from its dams in Quebec and to export markets in the United States and Ontario.

facts.t: Hydro-Québec reported net income of $2.9 billion for 2025, up 9% from 2024.

In January 2025 the Quebec Superior Court found that Hydro-Québec acted in institutional bad faith toward the Innu of Uashat and Mani-Utenam, failing to honour an agreement reached during the development of the La Romaine complex, and ordered it to pay $5 million in compensation.
Its US subsidiary H.Q. Energy Services (U.S.) did not file its own 2025 federal lobbying reports; two outside firms reported $350,000 in fees from it under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

hyundai.what: A South Korean carmaker established in 1967 and based in Seoul, which owns the Genesis brand and 33.88 per cent of Kia.
hyundai.money: Car sales: revenue of KRW 186.3 trillion and net profit of KRW 10.36 trillion in 2025.
hyundai.arts: Its Hyundai Artlab team runs long-term partnerships with Tate, LACMA, the Whitney Museum and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

hyundaimotor.money: Hyundai Motor’s money comes from making and financing cars.

facts.t: Hyundai Motor Company’s Brussels office declared EU lobbying costs of €600,000 to €699,999 for 2025, with 2.35 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Hyundai Motor Group a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Hyundai Motor Company reported $1,960,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

ianpotter.money: The Ian Potter Foundation was set up in 1964 by Sir Ian Potter, a financier and stockbroker, who was its founder and main benefactor.

iberdrola.money: Iberdrola's money comes from generating, distributing and selling electricity, and selling gas, in Spain, the UK (ScottishPower), the US and Brazil.

facts.t: Iberdrola closed 2025 with a record profit of 6.285 billion euros.
Iberdrola declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
InfluenceMap gives Iberdrola a B- grade for its climate policy engagement.

ibm.money: IBM's money comes from software, IT consulting and computer hardware, the mainframe among it.

facts.t: IBM reported 2025 revenue of $67.5 billion.
IBM reported $3,630,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

ihstowers.money: IHS Towers’ money comes from leasing telecom towers, mainly in Nigeria, where IHS Nigeria is its arm.

ikea.money: IKEA's money comes from selling furniture and home goods: Inter IKEA owns the brand and franchises it, and the Ingka group runs most IKEA stores; Ingvar Kamprad founded IKEA.

facts.t: Disclose reported in November 2022 that several Belarusian companies that worked for IKEA over the past ten years used forced labour in penal colonies holding political prisoners.
Inter IKEA Systems B.V. declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for September 2024 to August 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Ingka Services A.B., of the Ingka group that runs most IKEA stores, declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for September 2024 to August 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Outside firms reported $220,000 in 2025 fees for US federal lobbying from IKEA companies under the Lobbying Disclosure Act: $200,000 from IKEA US Retail and $20,000 from Inter IKEA Systems.

imls.what: An independent US federal agency established in 1996 by the Museum and Library Services Act; the main source of federal support for US libraries and museums.
imls.arts: In 2024 it awarded $266.7 million through grantmaking, research and policy work.
