imperialoil.money: Imperial’s money comes from oil sands mining (Kearl, and a share of Syncrude), refining and Esso fuel; ExxonMobil holds a majority of its shares.

facts.t: Imperial reported net income of $3,268 million for 2025, against $4,790 million in 2024.
In August 2024 Imperial Oil was fined $50,000 over the wastewater leak at its Kearl oil sands mine.

infosys.money: Infosys's money comes from IT services and consulting.

facts.t: Infosys delivered $19,277 million in FY25 revenues, growth of 4.2% in constant currency.
In 2013 Infosys agreed to pay US$34 million to end a US investigation into its use of temporary visas to fly workers to client sites in the United States; it denied widespread wrongdoing.
An outside firm, DGA Group Government Relations, reported $360,000 in 2025 fees from Infosys for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

ing.money: ING's money comes from retail and wholesale banking in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and other countries.

facts.t: ING Group reported FY2025 total income of €23,035 million and a net result of €6,327 million.

In September 2018 ING Bank paid a €775 million settlement to the Dutch Public Prosecution Service, which accused it of failing to prevent accounts of its Dutch clients from being used to launder hundreds of millions of euros between 2010 and 2016.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks ING Group 28th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of +$1.2 billion (+11.3%) from 2024.
ING Group declared EU lobbying costs of €600,000 to €699,999 for 2024, its last closed year on the register to the EU Transparency Register, with 2.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

inpex.money: INPEX is a Tokyo oil and gas producer whose Australian business runs the Ichthys LNG project.

facts.t: INPEX reported revenue of ¥2,011,351 million and profit attributable to owners of the parent of ¥393,836 million for the year to 31 December 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, INPEX Operations Australia Pty Ltd disclosed $180,950 in political donations: $75,950 to Labor branches and $105,000 to Liberal and National branches.

institutfranais.what: France's public agency for cultural diplomacy, a state industrial and commercial body set up in 2011 under the foreign and culture ministries; seated in Paris.
institutfranais.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Culture.
institutfranais.arts: It supports French artists and creative industries abroad and coordinates France's cultural network of more than 150 branches.

interceramic.money: Interceramic’s money comes from making and selling ceramic floor and wall tiles in Mexico and the United States.

intesasanpaolo.money: Intesa Sanpaolo's money comes from banking, insurance and asset management; it is Italy's largest bank.

facts.t: Intesa Sanpaolo reported net income of €9,321 million for 2025, up 7.6% from €8,666 million in 2024.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Intesa Sanpaolo 40th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of -$27 million (-0.6%) from 2024.
Intesa Sanpaolo declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 3 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

ireneludwig.what: A charitable foundation under German civil law, set up in Aachen in 1997 by Irene Ludwig from the foundation she and Peter Ludwig had founded in 1982.
ireneludwig.money: The art collection and fortune of Peter and Irene Ludwig; Peter Ludwig built up the chocolate maker Leonard Monheim, later Ludwig Schokolade.
ireneludwig.arts: It buys, manages and lends works for the Ludwig museums and supports exhibitions; a 2017 contract with the City of Cologne covers its work with Museum Ludwig.

isabeldossantos.money: Isabel dos Santos’s money comes from large stakes in Angolan companies in banking, telecoms and supermarkets; she is the daughter of Angola’s former president, and Sindika Dokolo, the foundation’s founder, was her husband.

facts.t: In January 2020 The Art Newspaper gave Forbes’s estimate of Isabel dos Santos’s personal fortune as $2.2 billion.
In July 2020 a Luanda court called a deal between Angola’s state diamond company and Sindika Dokolo “fraudulent” and harmful to ordinary Angolans (Luanda Leaks).
In December 2023 London’s High Court granted Unitel a worldwide order freezing up to £580m of her assets, in its suit over loans made while she was a Unitel director.
In November 2024 the UK sanctioned her under its anti-corruption regime; the Foreign Office said she stands accused of embezzling at least £350m from state-run firms.

ishibashi.money: The Ishibashi Foundation’s money comes from Bridgestone, the tyre maker Shojiro Ishibashi founded, chiefly through its holdings of investment securities.

facts.t: Bridgestone reported 2025 revenue of about 4,429.5 billion yen and net income of 327.3 billion yen.

In February 2014 Bridgestone agreed to plead guilty and pay a $425 million US criminal fine for fixing prices of anti-vibration rubber car parts; it had pleaded guilty in 2011 in a separate marine hose case.

ita.money: Itaú’s money comes from banking through Itaú Unibanco: lending, cards, insurance and asset management, mainly in Brazil.

facts.t: Itaú Unibanco closed 2024 with a record profit of R$41.403 billion.
One outside firm, Arnold & Porter, reported $140,000 in 2025 fees from Banco Itaú International for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

itsincludesoilrefinertpra.money: The Koç family’s money comes from Koç Holding, a Turkish group in energy (the Tüpraş refineries), cars, home appliances and finance.

facts.t: Koç Holding reported consolidated revenue of $65.8 billion for 2024, with $4.4 billion of combined investment.
In 2013 Koç Holding faced tax audits and lost a major naval defence contract after a hotel it owns sheltered Gezi Park protesters fleeing riot police, The Art Newspaper reported.

jackman.money: The Jackman family’s money comes from E-L Financial, the Toronto insurance and investment holding company of Hal Jackman.

jameel.money: The Jameel family’s money comes from Abdul Latif Jameel, founded in 1945, which began as Toyota’s distributor in Saudi Arabia and now works in mobility, energy, water, finance, health and investments.

facts.t: Forbes Middle East ranked Abdul Latif Jameel first among the Top 100 Arab Family Businesses of 2024; it operates in over 35 countries with more than 11,000 employees.

janetbuxton.what: The philanthropic foundation of the Melbourne art collectors Michael and Janet Buxton, through which they founded Buxton Contemporary at the University of Melbourne.
janetbuxton.money: The Buxtons' own wealth. Michael Buxton co-founded the Melbourne property developer MAB Corporation with Andrew Buxton in 1995.
janetbuxton.arts: In 2014 it gave the university their collection of contemporary Australian art and funds to build the gallery, which opened in 2018.

japan.what: A Japanese public body for international cultural exchange, set up in 1972 by an Act of the Diet, an Independent Administrative Institution since 2003.
japan.money: The Japanese state, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which oversees it.

japantobacco.what: A Japanese tobacco company set up in 1985 to take over the state tobacco monopoly and parent of Japan Tobacco International. By law the government owns at least one third.
japantobacco.money: Tobacco sales, which drove most of its growth: revenue of 3.47 trillion yen in 2025, up 13.4 percent.

javett.money: The Javett family gives through the Javett Foundation, a trust Michael Javett set up in 2013 to consolidate his and his family’s giving; the records do not say how the money was made.

jbwere.money: JBWere (NZ) Limited, a New Zealand wealth manager, uses the JBWere brand under licence from National Australia Bank's JBWere and is not a member of the NAB group.

jindal.money: Sangeeta Jindal's money comes through the JSW Foundation, of the JSW group, which is mostly steel; its power arm is about 5% of group revenue.

facts.t: JSW Steel reported a net profit of Rs 3,491 crore for FY25, down more than 61 per cent.
An outside firm, The Vogel Group, reported $187,000 in 2025 fees from JSW Steel USA for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

jpmorgan.what: The largest US bank, formed in 2000 by the merger of J.P. Morgan & Co. and Chase Manhattan, headquartered at 270 Park Avenue, New York.
jpmorgan.money: Interest and fees from consumer, commercial and investment banking: net income was $57.0 billion in 2025.

jpmorganchase.money: JPMorganChase’s money comes from consumer and commercial banking, investment banking and asset management.

facts.t: JPMorgan Chase declared EU lobbying costs of €1,000,000 to €1,249,999 for 2025, with 0.9 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
JPMorgan Chase reported $4,380,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
JPMorgan Chase’s federal PAC gave $723,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 46% to Republicans and 52% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

jti.money: JTI’s money comes from making and selling cigarettes and other tobacco products for its parent, Japan Tobacco.

facts.t: Japan Tobacco reported revenue of ¥3,149.8 billion for 2024, up 10.9%.
JT International Holding declared EU lobbying costs of €2,250,000 to €2,499,999 for 2025, with 6 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Japan Tobacco recorded a ¥400 billion provision in 2024 for its Canadian unit’s share of a C$32.5 billion tobacco litigation settlement.
Japan Tobacco International U.S.A. reported $590,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

juliusbaer.money: Julius Baer's money comes from private banking and wealth management.

facts.t: Bank Julius Baer & Co. Ltd declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

kajima.money: Kajima’s money comes from general construction, civil engineering and property development.

facts.t: In September 2026 Japan’s Supreme Court dismissed Kajima Corporation’s appeal in the maglev bid-rigging case, finalising a 250 million yen fine and a suspended prison sentence for a former senior official.

kamellazaar.money: Kamel Lazaar’s money comes from Swicorp, the investment banking, private equity and asset management firm he founded in 1987, headquartered in Riyadh.

kao.money: Kao’s money comes from consumer goods (detergents, toiletries, cosmetics) and chemicals; the tie is the Kao Foundation for Arts and Sciences.

kaspersky.money: Antivirus and cybersecurity software sold worldwide by a company founded in Moscow in 1997 by Eugene Kaspersky and others.

facts.t: The US Treasury sanctioned twelve Kaspersky Lab executives and leaders, the Commerce Department barred its products from the US and put AO Kaspersky Lab on the Entity List for cooperation with Russian military and intelligence authorities.

kering.money: Kering's money comes from luxury fashion and leather goods, Gucci, Saint Laurent and Bottega Veneta among its houses; the Pinault family's comes from Groupe Artémis, its holding company, which holds the family's Kering stake.

facts.t: Kering reported 2025 revenue of €14.7 billion, down 13% as reported, and net income from continuing operations attributable to the group of minus €29 million.

In May 2019 Kering agreed to pay €1.25 billion to settle a dispute with the Italian tax authorities over its Swiss subsidiary Luxury Goods International; the authorities accused Gucci of evading taxes on more than €1 billion of revenue between 2011 and 2017.
InfluenceMap gives Kering a B grade for its climate policy engagement.
Kering declared EU lobbying costs of €25,000 to €49,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

kerrystokes.money: Kerry Stokes’s money comes from his private company Australian Capital Equity and from SGH (formerly Seven Group Holdings), whose businesses include WesTrac, Boral, Coates and Beach Energy.

facts.t: SGH, the Kerry Stokes-led company, reported revenue of $10.7 billion and statutory net profit after tax of $486 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Australian Capital Equity Pty Limited, Kerry Stokes’s private holding company, disclosed $1,000,000 in political donations: $500,000 to Labor branches and $500,000 to Liberal and National branches.

kingstownbank.money: King's Town Bank's money comes from commercial banking in southern Taiwan.

facts.t: SinoPac Financial Holdings began counting King's Town Bank's profit from October 2025, after taking it over; SinoPac reported a 2025 after-tax net profit of NT$26.502 billion.
In its first quarter inside SinoPac Financial Holdings, King's Town Bank contributed NT$1.22 billion of investment income to the holding company, which reported 2025 net revenue of NT$74.39 billion.

kirsh.money: The Kirsh family’s money comes from Nathan Kirsh’s businesses; his Kirsh Group holds a majority of Jetro Holdings (Restaurant Depot, Jetro Cash and Carry).

facts.t: A Mail & Guardian comment of April 2018 said Nathan Kirsh is the largest shareholder and a former director of Magal Security Systems, which it said supplies perimeter control systems for the West Bank wall.

klm.money: Air France-KLM's money comes from passenger flights, cargo and aircraft maintenance.

facts.t: Air France-KLM declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

kulturstiftungdesbundes.what: An independent foundation set up in 2002 with seat in Halle an der Saale that funds contemporary art and culture across Germany and abroad.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.money: German federal funds: an annual budget of 35 million euros.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.arts: Since 2002 it has run over 40 funding programmes and backed about 4,000 projects, with multi-year support for documenta and the Berliner Theatertreffen.

kumhoasiana.money: Kumho Asiana Group’s money came from Asiana Airlines, construction (Kumho E&C) and tyres, under the Park family.

facts.t: In August 2022 a Seoul court sentenced former Kumho Asiana chairman Park Sam-koo to 10 years in prison for embezzlement and breach of trust; in September 2025 the Seoul High Court cleared him of those charges and gave him a suspended sentence for breaking the Fair Trade Act.

kunststiftungnrw.what: A public-law foundation set up on 12 September 1989 by the North Rhine-Westphalia state government under Johannes Rau, based in the Haus der Stiftungen in Düsseldorf.
kunststiftungnrw.money: The proceeds of the lottery operator WestLotto.
kunststiftungnrw.arts: It has funded about 12,000 projects in literature, music, performing arts and visual art with a link to North Rhine-Westphalia since 1989.

lacaixa.money: The "la Caixa" Foundation's budget comes from the dividends its holding CriteriaCaixa receives from its stakes in companies, CaixaBank first among them, with Naturgy, Telefónica and others.

facts.t: CaixaBank reported a net profit of 5,891 million euros for 2025, up 1.8%.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 reports that CaixaBank diluted its coal commitments in the past year, backtracking on metallurgical coal used for steelmaking.
CaixaBank declared EU lobbying costs of €600,000 to €699,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

lambent.what: A New York grantmaker for art, culture and social justice founded by the artist Anne Delaney, grown out of her Starry Night Fund of 2002.
lambent.money: Anne Delaney's philanthropy, held as a fiscally sponsored project of the Tides Center, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
lambent.arts: It funds contemporary art and culture tied to social justice in New York City, New Orleans and Nairobi.

langhamhotels.money: Langham's money comes from hotels, run by Langham Hospitality Group, part of Hong Kong's Great Eagle Holdings.

lassonde.money: Pierre Lassonde’s money comes from gold mining finance: he co-founded the royalty company Franco-Nevada and led Newmont.

lauder.money: The Lauder fortune comes from the Estée Lauder Companies, which sell cosmetics, skincare and fragrance.

facts.t: The Estée Lauder Companies reported net sales of $14,326 million for the fiscal year to June 2025, down from $15,608 million.

Leonard Lauder gave $248,100 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to Senate Impact Project ($23,100), New York State Democratic Committee ($10,000) and Arizona Democratic Party ($10,000), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

lavazza.money: Lavazza's money comes from roasting and selling coffee; the Lavazza family owns the group.

facts.t: Luigi Lavazza S.p.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €50,000 to €99,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 1.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

lazraq.money: The Lazraq family’s money comes from Groupe Alliances, the listed Moroccan property developer Alami Lazraq founded in 1994.

facts.t: Alliances reported consolidated revenue of 2.363 billion dirhams for 2024, up 17%, and consolidated net income of 305 million dirhams.

leechin.money: Michael Lee-Chin’s money comes from AIC mutual funds and Portland Holdings, his investment company.

lekoilnigeria.money: Lekoil’s money comes from oil exploration and production in Nigeria.

lendlease.money: Lendlease is a Sydney property developer, builder and investment manager.

leonidmikhelsonvac.money: Leonid Mikhelson’s money comes from Novatek, the gas producer of which he is chairman and major shareholder.

leonjimenes.money: The León Jimenes family’s money comes from tobacco, through the La Aurora cigar company its founder set up in 1903, and from beer.

facts.t: In 2012 E. León Jimenes sold 41.76% of the Cervecería Nacional Dominicana to AmBev for US$1 billion in cash, keeping a minority stake.

levistrauss.money: Levi Strauss & Co.'s money comes from selling jeans and other clothing.

facts.t: Levi Strauss & Co.'s revenue was $6,282 million in its fiscal year to November 2025.
Outside firms reported $230,000 in 2025 fees from Levi Strauss & Company for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; it filed no in-house report.
Levi Strauss & Co declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for its year from December 2024 to November 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

lg.money: LG’s money here comes from LG Electronics, which makes televisions, home appliances, vehicle parts and air conditioning.

facts.t: LG Electronics reported 2025 consolidated revenue of KRW 89.2 trillion and operating profit of KRW 2.48 trillion.
In December 2012 the European Commission fined LG Electronics €295.6 million for its part in two cathode ray tube cartels, and LG and Philips a further €392 million jointly.

linbury.what: A UK grant-making trust, one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, set up by Lord Sainsbury of Preston Candover and the ballerina Anya Linden, first granting in 1973.
linbury.money: Investment income and donations; it held funds of £135.0 million at 5 April 2025.
linbury.arts: In the year to April 2025 it paid £3.7 million to culture, including £2.25 million to the National Gallery's Sainsbury Wing.

lionfoundation.money: A gaming trust: its money is what players lose on the pokie machines it runs in pubs and hotels, which such trusts are required to give out, 40 percent of revenue by its own account, to community groups.

facts.t: The Department of Internal Affairs laid five charges of breaching the Gambling Act against the Lion Foundation over how much it knew of a person's use of pokie grants to benefit Southland Rugby and an Invercargill restaurant.
Its former chief executive David Conroy was found guilty of false accounting over journal entries made in 2002 to 2004 in the Lion Foundation accounts, in a case brought by the Serious Fraud Office.
Conroy was sentenced to 12 months' home detention and 300 hours of community work.

liuyiqian.money: Liu Yiqian and Wang Wei's fortune comes from his share trading and his companies, Sunline Group and Guohua Life Insurance, which he chairs and cofounded.

facts.t: Guohua Life Insurance, which Liu Yiqian chairs and cofounded, announced losses of between $23.3m and $28.7m for the first half of 2023.

liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Liverpool, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, under Labour control since 2010, with main offices in the Cunard Building.
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.money: Business rates (£295.1m), council tax (£277.0m) and general government grants (£245.5m) in its 2026-27 budget, £1.8bn gross.

lkab.money: LKAB’s money comes from iron ore mined at Kiruna and Malmberget; the Swedish state has owned all of it since 1976.

facts.t: Mining destabilised the ground under Kiruna and put the town at risk of collapse; LKAB proposed moving the town 3 km east and had allocated about SEK 12 billion to it.

lockheedmartin.money: Lockheed Martin's money comes from making weapons, military aircraft, missiles and space systems, most of it sold to the US government and its allies.

facts.t: Lockheed Martin reported 2025 sales of $75.0 billion and net earnings of $5.0 billion.

Bellingcat recorded 79 geolocated incidents in Gaza where remnants of US-made munitions, among them the Hellfire missile Lockheed Martin makes, were found after strikes, many of which caused death and damage to schools, homes and healthcare buildings.
Lockheed Martin reported $15,550,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act (an amended second-quarter report counted once).

loterieromande.what: A public-benefit lottery and sports betting company created in 1937 under an agreement between the governments of the French-speaking Swiss cantons, based in Lausanne; Jura joined in 1979.
loterieromande.money: Lottery and sports betting: gross gaming revenue was CHF 429.8 million in 2025, and its whole profit, CHF 252 million, went to associations.
loterieromande.arts: Its profit goes to associations in culture, social welfare, health, research, education, the environment, tourism, heritage and sport.

lucas.money: George Lucas's money comes from Lucasfilm, the Star Wars studio he sold to Disney in 2012; Mellody Hobson is co-CEO of Ariel Investments.

facts.t: Forbes says George Lucas sold Lucasfilm to Disney in 2012 for $4.1 billion in stock and cash, and put his net worth at $5.5 billion on 17 November 2026.

luce.money: The Henry Luce Foundation was set up by Henry R. Luce, co-founder of Time, Fortune and Life, and lives on its endowment.

facts.t: The Henry Luce Foundation reported total assets of $1,090,872,427 at the end of 2023 and $48,012,564 in grants paid that year, in its Form 990-PF.

ludwig.what: A foundation in Aachen set up in 1997 by Irene Ludwig, a year after the death of her husband Peter Ludwig, to place their collection in public museums.
ludwig.money: The fortune of Irene and Peter Ludwig, who ran the Monheim chocolate company until its sale in 1986, then Ludwig Schokolade until 1998.

lukoil.money: Lukoil’s money comes from oil and gas: exploration, production, refining and sales in Russia and abroad.

facts.t: On 22 October 2025 the US Treasury designated Lukoil and Rosneft, Russia’s two largest oil companies, with a number of their Russian subsidiaries.

luma.what: A Zurich non-profit set up in 2004 by Maja Hoffmann to support contemporary artists; it created the LUMA Arles arts campus, launched in 2013.
luma.money: Its founder Maja Hoffmann belongs to the shareholder pool of Roche founder descendants, which controls Roche Holding.

lvmhlouisvuitton.money: LVMH's money comes from selling luxury goods, wines and spirits, fashion, perfume, watches and jewellery (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Moët Hennessy, Bulgari and others); Bernard Arnault and his family control the group.

facts.t: LVMH reported 2025 revenue of €80,807 million and net profit (Group share) of €10,878 million.

In December 2021 a Paris court validated a settlement under which LVMH pays €10 million, ending an inquiry opened in 2011 into claims that it hired the former French domestic intelligence chief Bernard Squarcini to spy on private citizens, in particular the filmmaker François Ruffin.
LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 5.7 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton Inc. paid the outside firm S-3 Group $240,000 for US federal lobbying in 2025 (four quarterly reports of $60,000 under the Lobbying Disclosure Act); Moët Hennessy USA reported $215,000 of its own in-house spending.

mackelvie.money: The bequest of James Tannock Mackelvie (1824 to 1885), a businessman who kept an interest in Auckland affairs after returning to Britain; the trust still buys works for the collection.

macquarie.money: Macquarie Group is a Sydney investment bank and asset manager.

facts.t: Macquarie Group reported a net profit after tax of $A3,715 million for the year to 31 March 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Macquarie Group Limited disclosed $205,483 in political donations: $103,543 to Labor branches and $101,940 to Liberal and National branches.

manitobaartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Province of Manitoba, established in 1965, that makes awards to professional artists and arts organisations through peer assessment.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.money: The Manitoba provincial budget, through the department of Sport, Culture, Heritage and Tourism.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.arts: Its budget was C$12.7 million in 2023.

mapfre.money: Mapfre's money comes from insurance and reinsurance in Spain, Latin America and elsewhere; Fundación MAPFRE controls the listed company and lives on its dividends.

facts.t: Mapfre reported a 2025 net result of €1,078 million, up from €901.6 million, on premiums of €29,144.7 million.
MAPFRE S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €500,000 to €599,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.what: The public arts funding body of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, based in Boston, which makes grants to cultural organizations, schools, communities and individual artists.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.money: An annual appropriation from the Massachusetts Legislature, plus funds from the National Endowment for the Arts.

massy.money: Massy’s money comes from a Trinidad and Tobago group of industrial gases, motors and machinery, and retail across the Caribbean.

facts.t: Massy’s third-party revenue rose 3% to TT$15.8 billion in the year to September 2025, and profit before tax from continuing operations rose 4% to TT$1.1 billion.

mastercard.money: Mastercard runs a global card payments network and takes fees on the transactions.

facts.t: In January 2019 the European Commission fined Mastercard €570,566,000 for limiting merchants' access to better conditions offered by banks elsewhere in the Single Market, in breach of EU antitrust rules.
Mastercard Worldwide reported $5,440,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Mastercard Europe declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

mazda.what: A Japanese carmaker founded on 30 January 1920 as Toyo Cork Kogyo by Jujiro Matsuda, headquartered in Fuchu, Hiroshima Prefecture.
mazda.money: Sales of cars and commercial vehicles: net sales of 4,918.2 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

megacable.money: Megacable’s money comes from cable television, internet and telephone services in Mexico.

facts.t: Megacable’s sales were 35,430 million pesos in 2025 and its net profit 2,840 million pesos (Análisis B×+ annual table).

mellon.money: The Andrew W. Mellon Foundation's endowment comes from the fortune of the Pittsburgh banker and industrialist Andrew W. Mellon, through his children Paul Mellon and Ailsa Mellon Bruce; the Paul Mellon Centre, part of Yale, and the Richard King Mellon Foundation of Pittsburgh are other Mellon family money named in these entries.

facts.t: The Andrew W. Mellon Foundation reported total assets of $8,027,994,221 at the end of 2023 and paid $549,292,394 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).
The Richard King Mellon Foundation reported total assets of $2,601,768,833 at the end of 2023 and paid $112,236,615 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).

mendozafamily.money: The Mendoza family’s money came from the companies of Eugenio Mendoza Goiticoa, a Venezuelan industrialist.

mercedesbenz.money: Mercedes-Benz's money comes from making and selling cars and vans, and from car finance.

facts.t: Mercedes-Benz reported net profit of 5.3 billion euros for 2025, down almost 49 percent from 2024, AFP reported.
In a US settlement filed in September 2020 over undisclosed defeat devices in about 250,000 diesel vehicles, Daimler AG and Mercedes-Benz USA agreed to a recall and a civil penalty of $875 million.
Mercedes-Benz Group AG declared EU lobbying costs of €1,750,000 to €1,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Mercedes-Benz USA reported $1,365,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Mercedes-Benz a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.

methanex.money: Methanex, a Canadian company, makes methanol from natural gas at plants in the United States, Trinidad, New Zealand and elsewhere.

facts.t: Full year 2025 net income attributable to Methanex shareholders was $80 million, with Adjusted EBITDA of $808 million.
Bracewell LLP registered to lobby the US federal government for Methanex in the fourth quarter of 2025 and reported $40,000 in income from it.

michaelaudain.what: A Canadian home builder and art collector, born in 1937, chairman since 1992 and a major shareholder of Polygon Homes Ltd. in Vancouver.
michaelaudain.money: His stake in Polygon Homes; he gives mainly through the Audain Foundation, which he set up in 1997 with Yoshiko Karasawa.
michaelaudain.arts: The Audain Foundation funds the annual C$100,000 Audain Prize for the Visual Arts and gave C$2 million to Arts Umbrella in 2023.

midea.money: The He family's fortune comes from Midea Group, the home appliance maker He Xiangjian founded.

facts.t: Midea Group reported 2024 revenue of RMB 409.1 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 38.5 billion.
The Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported in August 2025 that Midea owns factories linked to China's Uyghur labour transfer scheme; Midea did not respond.
One outside firm reported $30,000 in 2025 fees from Midea America for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

minderoo.money: Minderoo Foundation is Andrew and Nicola Forrest’s philanthropy, funded from their iron ore company Fortescue; in 2023 they gave it Fortescue shares worth $5 billion.

facts.t: Fortescue reported a net profit after tax of US$3.4 billion and underlying EBITDA of US$7.9 billion for the year to 30 June 2025.

In May 2026 the Federal Court awarded the Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation $150.1 million in native title compensation over the mining tenements for Fortescue’s Solomon Hub, $150 million of it for cultural loss, the highest such award to date.

ministredelaculture|France.what: France's culture ministry, created in 1959 by President Charles de Gaulle for André Malraux, with offices on the rue de Valois in Paris and regional offices (DRAC).
ministredelaculture|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

ministryofocw|Netherlands.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science, created in 1918 and based in The Hague.
ministryofocw|Netherlands.money: The Dutch state budget, with €618 million a year in 2025-2028 for culture paid through the national cultural infrastructure and six national culture funds.

minsheng.money: Ningxia Minsheng Group is a regional property developer in Ningxia.

facts.t: In 2015 Ningxia Minsheng Group planned to invest $5bn over the next decade in Huaxia-Hetu Art Town, the 18.8 sq. km development MoCA Yinchuan anchors.

mirvac.money: Mirvac is a Sydney property developer and landlord of offices, shopping centres and housing.

mitsubishi.money: The ties name separate Mitsubishi companies, mostly Mitsubishi Electric (electrical and industrial equipment), and also Mitsubishi Motors, Mitsubishi Chemical and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical.

facts.t: An outside committee’s final report in October 2022 found 197 cases of improper quality inspections at Mitsubishi Electric sites in Japan.

mitsui.money: The ties name Mitsui Fudosan, a Tokyo property developer, and Mitsui & Co., a trading house; they are separate companies of the Mitsui group.

facts.t: In September 2023 ICOMOS issued a Heritage Alert over the Meiji Jingu Gaien redevelopment in Tokyo, of which Mitsui Fudosan is a major developer; the developers planned to cut down 743 trees.

mittal.money: Lakshmi Mittal's money comes from ArcelorMittal, the steel and mining company his family controls; his son Aditya Mittal is its chief executive.

facts.t: ArcelorMittal reported net income attributable to equity holders of US$3,152 million for 2025, on sales of US$61,352 million.
A fire at the Kostenko coal mine in Kazakhstan, operated by ArcelorMittal Temirtau, killed 45 people on 28 October 2023.
ArcelorMittal declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for its closed financial year, February 2025 to January 2026.
ArcelorMittal North America Holdings reported $880,000 in its own 2025 US federal lobbying reports, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap scores ArcelorMittal D+ for its climate policy engagement.

mizuho.money: Mizuho’s money comes from banking, securities and trust business.

facts.t: Japan’s Financial Services Agency issued Mizuho a business improvement order in November 2021 over repeated system failures, and its chief executive Tatsufumi Sakai said he would step down.

molson.money: The Molson family’s money comes from Molson Coors, the brewer the family controls with the Coors family, given through the Molson Foundation.

mondotv.money: Mondo TV’s money comes from producing and selling animated programmes, much of the animation work outsourced.

facts.t: In June 2024 Mondo TV agreed to pay $538,000 to settle 18 apparent violations of US sanctions on North Korea, for about $537,939 paid between May 2019 and November 2021 for animation work outsourced to a North Korean state-owned studio.

mondriaan.what: The Dutch public fund for visual art and cultural heritage, formed in Amsterdam in 2012 by merging the Mondriaan Stichting (set up 1994) with Fonds BKVB.
mondriaan.money: The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.
mondriaan.arts: In 2024 it approved 2,257 of 4,204 applications, awarding 53,438,678 euros in total.

moody.money: The Moody Foundation of Galveston was founded in 1942 by William Lewis Moody Jr. and Libbie Rice Shearn Moody; Wikipedia gives its main revenue as dividends on American National Insurance Company stock.

mordant.money: Simon Mordant’s money comes from investment banking: he founded the corporate advisory firm Caliburn, which merged with Greenhill & Co. in 2010.

mordashov.money: Alexei Mordashov’s money comes from Severstal, the steel and mining company he controls.

morganstanley.money: Morgan Stanley is a US investment bank and wealth manager.

facts.t: Morgan Stanley reported net revenues of $70.6 billion for 2025, against $61.8 billion a year earlier.
Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC reported $4,450,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Morgan Stanley declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

moribuilding.money: Mori Building’s money comes from developing and letting Tokyo property, such as Roppongi Hills, Toranomon Hills and Azabudai Hills.

facts.t: In September 2005 the Tokyo District Court found two former Mori Building officials and a door maker’s former director guilty of professional negligence over a six-year-old boy’s death in a revolving door at Roppongi Hills in March 2004; they avoided prison.

motiva.money: Motiva, formerly CCR, makes its money from toll road, urban rail and airport concessions in Brazil.

facts.t: In November 2018 CCR agreed to pay R$81.5 million to close a São Paulo prosecutors’ inquiry, begun after the Lava Jato informant Adir Assad said the company paid undeclared campaign money (caixa dois) to politicians of the PSDB, PMDB, PSD and PTB.

mphasis.money: Mphasis's money comes from IT services, mostly for banks and financial firms.

facts.t: Mphasis's net profit for the year ended March 2025 grew 9.5 per cent to Rs 1,702.1 crore, on revenue from operations of Rs 14,230 crore.

mtn.money: MTN’s money comes from mobile voice, data and mobile money services across Africa.

facts.t: MTN Group’s service revenue rose 22.9% to R218.5 billion in 2025, on a reported basis.

In June 2016 MTN Nigeria agreed to pay 330 billion naira ($1.671 billion at the official rate) to settle a fine first set at $5.2 billion for failing to disconnect unregistered phone lines by a regulator’s deadline.

In September 2026 a US federal court in New York let two Anti-Terrorism Act suits proceed to discovery; families of more than 200 US soldiers killed and wounded in Afghanistan claim MTN paid protection money to the Taliban, which MTN denies.
Two outside firms reported $590,000 in 2025 fees from MTN (Dubai) Limited for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

munjal.money: Sunil Kant Munjal's money comes from Hero Enterprise, which he chairs, his part of the Hero group, with firms in insurance broking and real estate.

murdoch.money: The tie here is Freelands Foundation, set up by Elisabeth Murdoch, daughter of Rupert Murdoch, whose family controls News Corp and Fox Corporation.

myer.money: The Sidney Myer Fund and the Myer Foundation come from the fortune of Sidney Myer, who founded the Myer department stores and died in 1934.

mykhaylova.money: Liubov Mykhaylova is a businesswoman who owns IZOLYATSIA; the sources do not say what her business is.

nab.money: National Australia Bank is one of Australia’s four major banks.

facts.t: NAB reported statutory net profit of $6,759 million and cash earnings of $7,091 million for the year to 30 September 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, National Australia Bank Limited disclosed $142,500 in political donations: $66,000 to Labor branches and $76,500 to Liberal and National branches.

nadar.money: The Nadar family’s money comes from HCL, the IT services group Shiv Nadar founded, chiefly HCLTech.

facts.t: HCLTech reported revenue of ₹117,055 crore, up 6.5%, and net income of ₹17,390 crore for the year to March 2025.
In March 2025 Shiv Nadar gifted 47% of his stake in HCL Corp and Vama Delhi to his daughter Roshni Nadar Malhotra, making her the majority shareholder of the family’s holding companies.

nanfung.money: Nan Fung Group began as a Hong Kong cotton spinner and now makes its money from property development, financial investment, life sciences and shipping.

nasher.money: The Nasher money comes from Raymond Nasher, a Dallas real estate developer who built NorthPark Center in the early 1960s, and the Nasher Foundation.

nationalbankcanada.money: National Bank of Canada’s money comes from banking, wealth management and capital markets, mostly in Quebec.

facts.t: National Bank reported fourth-quarter 2025 net income of $1.059 billion and full-year adjusted profit of $4.479 billion.

nationalendowmentforarts.what: An independent agency of the US federal government, created by Congress in 1965 and signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson; based in Washington, D.C.
nationalendowmentforarts.money: Annual appropriations from the US Congress: $207,000,000 a year for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.

nationallotteryheritage.what: The UK distributor of National Lottery money for heritage, set up in 1994 as the Heritage Lottery Fund and renamed in 2019; head office in London.
nationallotteryheritage.money: A share of National Lottery proceeds raised from players, plus heritage funding it distributes for the UK and devolved governments.
nationallotteryheritage.arts: Since 1994 it has awarded over £9.9 billion of National Lottery and other funding to more than 54,000 projects.

nationallottery|Belgium.what: Belgium's largest lottery operator, founded in 1934 as the Colonial Lottery and a public-law limited company since 2002, under the Federal Public Service Finance.
nationallottery|Belgium.money: Sales of its lottery games and Scooore sports betting; it pays a monopoly fee to the federal treasury.
nationallottery|Belgium.arts: Parliament decides which projects and organisations receive its yearly subsidies.

nationaltrustforhistoric.what: A privately funded nonprofit founded in 1949 by congressional charter and based in Washington, D.C.; it runs historic sites and campaigns to save historic places.
nationaltrustforhistoric.money: Contributions, 66.1% of US$104.9 million revenue in the year to June 2025, plus investment income and asset sales.

naturgy.money: Naturgy’s money comes from gas and electricity: supplying and distributing gas and power in Spain and Latin America, Panama among them.

facts.t: Naturgy’s net profit rose 6.4% to 2,023 million euros in 2025.
Naturgy Energy Group declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2024 to the EU Transparency Register.
Its US subsidiary Naturgy Candela Devco LLC paid SC Partners $80,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, as the firm reported.

neilson.money: The Neilson Foundation is funded by Kerr Neilson, founder of the fund manager Platinum Asset Management.

nesr.money: The Nesr family’s money comes from Webcor Group, one of Angola’s largest companies, which imports and distributes food; Wissam Nesr is its chief executive.

netflix.money: Netflix's money comes from streaming subscriptions and advertising.

facts.t: Netflix's revenue was $45,183 million in 2025.
Netflix, Inc. reported $3,080,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Netflix International B.V. declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

newcarlsberg.what: A private foundation for the arts set up by charter on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia, based in Copenhagen.
newcarlsberg.money: Dividends from Carlsberg A/S shares, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, and returns on its other investments.
newcarlsberg.arts: It donates artworks to Danish museums, commissions site-specific art (decorative projects) and gives art awards.

newfortress.money: New Fortress Energy’s money comes from importing and selling liquefied natural gas and from power generation, including Puerto Rico’s state power plants, which its subsidiary Genera PR operates.

facts.t: In May 2025 Puerto Rico’s Energy Bureau ordered Genera PR to cease converting the Palo Seco and Mayagüez units to natural gas, citing the risk of a supply monopoly favouring its parent, New Fortress Energy.
New Fortress Energy paid the firm H.A. Cumber & Company $160,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, as the firm reported.
Genera PR paid the firm Alta Crest $216,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, $54,000 a quarter, as the firm reported.

newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

nike.money: Nike designs and sells sports shoes, clothing and equipment, made by contract factories.

facts.t: Nike reported revenues of $46.3 billion for the year to May 2025, down 10%.
Nike, Inc reported $2,560,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Nike, Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €500,000 to €599,999 for June 2025 to May 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

nipponfoundation.money: The Nippon Foundation’s money comes from a share of the proceeds of betting on motorboat racing in Japan; the Great Britain Sasakawa Foundation bears the name of its founder, Ryoichi Sasakawa.

facts.t: Ryoichi Sasakawa, who built the motorboat racing business behind the foundation, was held in Sugamo Prison as a Class A war criminal suspect and released in 1948 without ever being indicted, according to the biography the foundation publishes.

nomura.money: Nomura’s money comes from securities brokerage, investment banking and asset management; the ties are Nomura Securities and the Nomura Foundation.

facts.t: In 2024 Japanese regulators fined Nomura Securities 21.76 million yen for manipulating 10-year Japanese government bond futures in March 2021.

nordea.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1989 by the savings bank Sparekassen SDS when it became a limited company, named Nordea-fonden since 2008.
nordea.money: Returns on its assets, chiefly a stake of about 4.4 percent in Nordea Bank Abp. It gives over 80 percent of yearly returns to charity.
nordea.arts: Culture is one of its four areas of support, alongside health, exercise and nature, with a grant pool for culture houses (Kulturhuspuljen).

northerntrust.money: Northern Trust is a Chicago bank for wealth management and asset servicing.

facts.t: Northern Trust Corporation reported $420,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.

northwestel.money: Northwestel’s money comes from telephone and internet service across Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut; Bell Canada has been its parent since 1988.

norval.money: Louis Norval’s money comes from property investment in South Africa.

nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.what: The unitary local authority for the city of Nottingham, under Labour control since 1991, with main offices at Loxley House.
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.money: UK government grants, including the Revenue Support Grant, and council tax.

novartis.money: Novartis's money comes from making and selling prescription medicines.

facts.t: In July 2020 Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation agreed to pay $678 million to settle a US fraud lawsuit over sham speaker programs through which it paid over $100 million to doctors to induce them to prescribe its drugs.
Novartis International AG declared EU lobbying costs of €2,500,000 to €2,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Novartis reported $7,788,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, amended figures used where filed.

novonordisk.money: Novo Nordisk's money comes from diabetes and obesity drugs (insulin, Ozempic, Wegovy); the Novo Nordisk Foundation, which gives the atlas ties here, controls the company through its holding company and draws on its dividends.

facts.t: Novo Nordisk reported 2025 net sales of DKK 309,064 million and net profit of DKK 102,434 million.

In January 2025 Novo Nordisk settled Minnesota's insulin pricing lawsuit by agreeing to cap the out-of-pocket cost of its insulin at $35 a month for five years and give free insulin to the neediest Minnesotans.
Novo Nordisk A/S declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Novo Nordisk Inc. reported $7,230,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

nrwcultureministry|Germany.what: The culture and science ministry of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia in Düsseldorf, led by Minister Ina Brandes.
nrwcultureministry|Germany.arts: In June 2026 it granted about 18 million euros to Kultur Ruhr GmbH for the Ruhrtriennale, Chorwerk Ruhr, Tanzlandschaft Ruhr and Urbane Künste Ruhr.

nswgovernment|Australia.what: The state government of New South Wales, Australia, led since March 2023 by the Labor Premier Chris Minns.
nswgovernment|Australia.money: The New South Wales state budget, which funds the arts through Create NSW and its Arts and Cultural Funding Program.

nubank.money: Nubank’s money comes from digital banking, credit cards and loans in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.

facts.t: Nu Holdings posted net income of $2.9 billion in 2025, against $2.0 billion in 2024.

nycarlsberg.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
nycarlsberg.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

nycarlsbergfondet.what: A Danish art foundation set up on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia Jacobsen, operating under the Carlsberg Foundation in Copenhagen.
nycarlsbergfondet.money: Mainly dividends from shares in the brewer Carlsberg A/S.
nycarlsbergfondet.arts: It funds visual art, applied art and architecture in Denmark, including gifts of works to museums and decorative commissions.

nycculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.what: The New York City agency that funds non-profit culture in the five boroughs, a separate city agency since 1976.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.money: New York City's budget: an operating budget of $300 million in fiscal 2026, almost entirely city money.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.arts: Its Cultural Development Fund gave $74.3 million to 1,171 organisations in fiscal 2026.

nysca.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
nysca.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
nysca.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

nzct.money: A gaming trust: its money comes from pokie machines that hospitality operators run in their hotels and bars, and it says it returns all its net profit, at least 40 percent of gross profit, as grants.

facts.t: In its 2024/25 financial year NZCT generated $36.334 million for communities and distributed $38.244 million through 1,992 grants.

oakfoundation.money: The Oak Foundation was founded in 1983 by the billionaire Alan M. Parker, co-founder of the duty-free company DFS Group.

obayashi.money: Obayashi’s money comes from general construction, civil engineering and property development.

facts.t: In October 2018 the Tokyo District Court fined Obayashi Corporation 200 million yen for rigging bids for maglev (Chuo Shinkansen) station works.

occidental.money: Occidental's money comes from oil and gas production, with chemicals through OxyChem.

facts.t: Occidental Petroleum's revenue was $21,593 million in 2025.
In 2013 Occidental reached a confidential settlement with Achuar Indigenous communities in Peru over 30 years of contamination of the Corrientes River basin.
Occidental paid $190 million in 2014 for the contamination of the Passaic River in New Jersey.
Occidental Petroleum Corporation reported $11,330,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Occidental Petroleum Corporation declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

octgroup.money: OCT Group (Overseas Chinese Town) is a central state-owned enterprise in tourism, theme parks and property.

facts.t: Overseas Chinese Town A, the group's Shenzhen-listed company, had revenue of 102.6 billion yuan in 2021, then a loss in 2022 and a net loss attributable to shareholders of 1.3 billion yuan in the first half of 2023.

ocw.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science in The Hague, led in 2026 by Minister Rianne Letschert.
ocw.money: The Dutch national budget: 57 billion euros of spending set for 2026.
ocw.arts: Its 2026 budget sets 2.7 billion euros for culture and media.

okayamagas.what: A city gas company founded in Okayama on 29 January 1910, supplying Okayama, Kurashiki, Akaiwa, Tamano, Soja and Hayashima.
okayamagas.money: Sales of city gas, gas appliances and pipe work; non-consolidated revenue was ¥24.81 billion in 2015.

omv.money: OMV's money comes from oil and gas production, refining and fuels, and chemicals.

facts.t: OMV reported 2025 sales from continuing operations of EUR 24.3 billion and a clean CCS Operating Result of EUR 4.6 billion.
InfluenceMap gives OMV a D+ grade for its climate policy engagement.
OMV Aktiengesellschaft declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

ontarioartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Ontario government, created by provincial law in 1963 under Premier John Robarts; based in Toronto.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.money: The Government of Ontario, through its culture ministry.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.arts: It runs more than fifty funding programmes for Ontario artists and arts organisations.

opensociety.what: A grantmaking network founded by investor George Soros, begun with a Budapest foundation in 1984; the Open Society Institute was set up in New York in 1993.
opensociety.money: George Soros's personal fortune: he had given over $32 billion by 2017, including an $18 billion transfer announced that year.

orange.money: Orange's money comes from telecommunications: mobile, broadband and business networks in France, Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

facts.t: Orange reported 2025 revenue of 40,396 million euros and consolidated net income of 1,139 million euros.
Orange declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

ortizgurdian.money: The Ortiz Gurdián family’s money comes from banking: Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga presides over Banpro, a bank of the Grupo Promerica financial group.

oyebode.money: Gbenga Oyebode’s money comes from law and business: he co-founded the law firm Aluko & Oyebode and chairs Okomu Oil Palm, in which he holds 4.37 percent.

paiz.money: The Paiz family’s money came from Almacenes Paiz, its chain of stores in Guatemala.

panasonic.money: Panasonic’s money comes from electronics, batteries, appliances and business systems such as Panasonic Connect.

facts.t: In April 2018 Panasonic and its in-flight entertainment unit Panasonic Avionics agreed to pay about $280 million to settle US charges under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

patino.money: The Patiño foundations’ money goes back to Simón I. Patiño’s tin mines in Bolivia, confiscated in the 1952 revolution; his heirs’ Geneva foundation manages the funds.

paulgettytrust.what: A trust founded in 1953 by J. Paul Getty, founder of Getty Oil, that runs the Getty Museum, Research Institute, Conservation Institute and Getty Foundation in Los Angeles.
paulgettytrust.money: An endowment of US$9.4 billion (2025) built on Getty's bequest, which included nearly $660 million in Getty Oil stock received in 1982.
paulgettytrust.arts: The Getty Foundation gives grants to museums and cultural institutions worldwide.

paulhamlyn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity started by publisher Paul Hamlyn in 1987 and in its current form since 2004; based in King's Cross, London.
paulhamlyn.money: An endowment from Paul Hamlyn's publishing fortune: a £50m gift in 1987 and about £308 million from his estate in 2001.
paulhamlyn.arts: It funds children and young people, with a focus on the arts.

perelman.money: Ronald Perelman's money comes from MacAndrews & Forbes, the holding company through which he bought and sold businesses from candy to cosmetics, Revlon among them.

facts.t: Forbes put Ronald Perelman's net worth at $1.5 billion in November 2026, and says he lost his Revlon holdings in its 2023 bankruptcy proceedings after selling billions of dollars of assets to pay debt in late 2020.

pernodricard.money: Pernod Ricard's money comes from making and selling spirits and wine: Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Martell and Ricard among its brands.

facts.t: Pernod Ricard reported net sales of €10,959m for its financial year to June 2025 and group net profit of €1,626m.
Pernod Ricard declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for its financial year July 2025 to June 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

Pernod Ricard reported $400,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for the first quarter of 2025, in a report that also ended its in-house registration; outside firms reported further fees from Pernod Ricard USA through the year.

petrobras.money: Petrobras’s money comes from producing, refining and selling oil and gas in Brazil.

facts.t: Petrobras ended 2024 with a net profit of R$36.6 billion (US$7.5 billion).

In 2018 Petrobras settled SEC charges that it misled US investors with false financial statements concealing a massive bribery and bid-rigging scheme, and took a non-prosecution agreement with the US Justice Department, agreeing to pay $933 million in disgorgement and interest and an $853 million penalty, subject to offsets.
InfluenceMap gives Petrobras a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.

pfizer.money: Pfizer's money comes from prescription medicines and vaccines.

facts.t: Pfizer's revenue was $62,579 million in 2025.

In September 2009 Pfizer agreed to pay $2.3 billion, then the largest health care fraud settlement, to resolve criminal and civil allegations that it illegally promoted four drugs, including the painkiller Bextra.
Pfizer Inc. reported $12,630,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Pfizer Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

philipmorris.money: Altria makes its money from cigarettes such as Marlboro in the United States, and from cigars, smokeless tobacco and nicotine products.

facts.t: Altria reported net revenues of about $24.0 billion for 2024, down 1.9%.
Philip Morris was among four tobacco companies in the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement, worth $206 billion to US states.
Altria reported $12,370,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
ALTRIAPAC, Altria’s PAC, gave $810,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 68% to Republicans and 30% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

phillips.what: An auction house founded in London in 1796, with head offices in London and New York and a UK holding company, Phillips Assets Ltd.
phillips.money: Fees on auction and private sales (UK turnover £89m in 2024), under a parent, Mercury Group Trading, controlled by Leonid Fridlyand and Leonid Strunin.

pictet.money: Pictet's money comes from private banking, wealth management and asset management; it is owned by its partners.

pinchuk.money: Victor Pinchuk’s money comes from Interpipe, the maker of steel pipes and railway wheels he founded in 1990, and from his investment group EastOne.

facts.t: Hogan Lovells reported $130,000 in 2025 fees from North American Interpipe for US federal lobbying on trade rules and duties, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

pingan.money: Ping An is an insurance and financial services group.

facts.t: Ping An Insurance reported 2024 revenue of RMB 1,141,346 million, and said net profit attributable to shareholders rose 47.8%.

pnc.what: A US bank holding company in Pittsburgh, tracing to the Pittsburgh Trust and Savings Company of 1845 and formed as PNC by a 1982 merger.
pnc.money: Interest and fees from personal, small business and corporate banking through PNC Bank; revenue was US$21.49 billion in 2023.

poddar.money: Abhishek Poddar's money comes from his family's companies: he is managing director of Matheson Bosanquet, in tea production, trading and export, and a director of Sua Explosives & Accessories, which makes mining explosives.

pola.money: The money came from the Pola cosmetics company and the Suzuki family that founded it; the foundation was set up with Tsuneji Suzuki’s personal assets.

polygonhomes.what: A Metro Vancouver home builder in business since 1980, chaired by its major shareholder Michael Audain.
polygonhomes.money: Sales of the homes it builds and develops, more than 35,000 to date, from masterplanned communities to high-rise towers.

power.what: A Canadian holding company founded in 1925 and based in Montreal, controlled since 1968 by a group led by Paul Desmarais.
power.money: Its financial services holdings in insurance, retirement, wealth and asset management, which have included Great-West Life, Canada Life, IGM Financial and Mackenzie.

powercorp.money: Power Corporation of Canada, controlled by the Desmarais family, draws its money from life insurance and wealth management (Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial) and from holdings in Europe through GBL.

facts.t: Power Corporation reported net earnings from continuing operations of $2,572 million for 2025, against $2,792 million in 2024.

prada.money: Prada's money comes from selling luxury fashion and leather goods (Prada, Miu Miu); Miuccia Prada and Patrizio Bertelli control the group.

facts.t: Prada Group reported 2024 net revenues of €5.4 billion, up 17% at constant currency, and Group net income of €839 million.

princeclaus.what: A Dutch fund set up in 1996 and named after Prince Claus of the Netherlands; it gives grants and awards to artists in places where culture is under pressure.
princeclaus.money: An annual subsidy from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
princeclaus.arts: Its Principal Award is worth €100,000; since 1996 it has supported almost 2,400 projects in 144 countries.

pritzkerfamily.money: The Pritzker family's money comes from family companies, among them Hyatt Hotels, which the family founded; its Hyatt Foundation sponsors the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

facts.t: Hyatt Hotels Corporation's revenue was $7,101 million in 2025.

prohelvetia.what: The Swiss Confederation's arts foundation, set up by the Federal Council in 1939 and made a foundation under public law in 1949; based in Zurich.
prohelvetia.money: The Swiss federal budget, set by parliament in four-year Cultural Messages: CHF 186.9 million for 2025 to 2028.
prohelvetia.arts: In 2025 it approved 2,448 of 7,235 applications and put 86.9 percent of its funds directly into art and culture.

prokhorov.money: Mikhail Prokhorov’s money comes from metals, through his former stake in Norilsk Nickel, and from his investment group Onexim.

promsvyazbank.money: PSB’s money comes from banking: a state-owned bank, nationalised in 2018, that the US Treasury calls critical to Russia’s defence sector.

facts.t: On 22 February 2022 the US Treasury sanctioned PSB and its subsidiaries, calling it critical to Russia’s defence sector, and designated its chairman and chief executive Petr Fradkov.

provinceofbc|Canada.what: The provincial government of British Columbia, Canada, led by a Premier and Cabinet answerable to the 93-member Legislative Assembly in Victoria.
provinceofbc|Canada.money: Provincial taxes, natural resource royalties and federal transfers; revenue was forecast at C$83.3 billion for 2025-26.

pubcharity.money: A gaming trust: its money is the revenue from the pokie machines it runs in pubs and bars, given out as grants for charitable purposes.

facts.t: In the year to 30 September 2025 Pub Charity reported revenue from gaming machines of $107,904 thousand, paid $24,818 thousand in gaming machine duty and distributed $45,333 thousand in grants.

pumaenergy.money: Trafigura’s money comes from trading oil, metals and minerals; Puma Energy, the fuel distributor it controls, sells fuel in Latin America, Africa and Asia.

facts.t: Trafigura was behind the 2006 dumping of toxic waste in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, after which over 100,000 people sought medical help (Amnesty International and Greenpeace Netherlands).

Trafigura pleaded guilty in the United States to conspiring to violate the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act in Brazil, with a criminal penalty of about $80.5 million and forfeiture of about $46.5 million.

Switzerland’s Federal Criminal Court found Trafigura guilty of “organizational failure” in relation to corruption in Angola, with a fine of CHF 3 million and a compensation claim of USD 145 million, for close to USD 5 million in bribes paid between 2009 and 2011.
Trafigura’s net profit was USD 2,666 million for the year to 30 September 2025, down three percent.
Trafigura Pte Ltd declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for October 2024 to September 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Trafigura Pte Ltd paid the firm Ragnar Group $160,000 for federal lobbying in 2025 ($80,000 in each of the third and fourth quarters), as the firm reported.

qantas.money: Qantas is Australia’s largest airline, with Jetstar and the Qantas loyalty business.

facts.t: The Qantas Group reported revenue and other income of $23,823 million and a statutory profit after tax of $1,605 million for the year to 30 June 2025.
In August 2025 the Federal Court ordered Qantas to pay a $90 million penalty for illegally outsourcing more than 1,800 ground staff in 2020, after its appeal to the High Court failed.

qatarmuseums.what: A Qatari government entity founded in 2005 that runs the country's museums, chaired by Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani under the Amir's patronage.
qatarmuseums.arts: It oversees the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf, the National Museum of Qatar and the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum.

qattan.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattan.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattan.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qiaozhibing.money: Qiao Zhibing's money comes from karaoke clubs in Shanghai.

quarkexpeditions.money: Polar expedition cruises; Quark is a member of the Travelopia group, which KKR agreed to buy from TUI in 2017.

facts.t: KKR agreed to buy Travelopia, the travel group Quark belongs to, from TUI; Travelopia then had 53 brands and over 800,000 travellers a year.

rabobank.money: Rabobank's money comes from banking, above all lending to farmers and the food and agriculture business; it is a Dutch cooperative bank.

facts.t: In October 2013 the US CFTC ordered Rabobank to pay a $475 million penalty for false reporting and attempted manipulation of LIBOR and Euribor; in related actions it agreed to a $325 million US Justice Department penalty, a £105 million UK FCA penalty and a €70 million payment to Dutch prosecutors.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Rabobank 48th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of -$212 million (-6.9%) from 2024.
Rabobank declared EU lobbying costs of €300,000 to €399,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 2.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

raiffeisen.money: Raiffeisen is not one company: the atlas ties name Swiss Raiffeisen banks (the Raiffeisen Switzerland cooperative group) and Austrian ones (Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberösterreich, Raiffeisen Salzburg), cooperative banks owned by their members.

rbc.money: RBC’s money comes from banking, wealth management, insurance and capital markets.

facts.t: RBC’s UK asset manager, RBC Global Asset Management (UK), declared EU lobbying costs of €10,000 to €24,999 for November 2024 to October 2025; the bank itself is not on the register.
RBC USA Holdco’s federal PAC gave $78,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 55% to Republicans and 45% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

realdania.what: A Danish member-based philanthropic association created in 2000, when Realkredit Danmark sold its mortgage business in its merger with Danske Bank, based in Copenhagen.
realdania.money: Returns on investing the capital it kept from that deal; about 195,000 members own it.
realdania.arts: It funds projects in architecture, planning and the built environment.

regionecampania.what: The regional government of Campania in southern Italy, seated in Naples and led by President Roberto Fico with a 60-member Regional Council.
regionecampania.money: The regional budget, over EUR 38.5 billion for 2026, almost 70% of it for health.
regionecampania.arts: Its 2026 budget raises cinema funding to EUR 6 million and live-performance funding to EUR 17 million.

regionelazio.what: The regional government of Lazio in central Italy, seated in Rome and led by President Francesco Rocca, with a Regional Council as its legislature.
regionelazio.money: The regional budget; its 2025 economic and financial plan set the 2025 to 2027 budget at about EUR 10 billion.

regionepiemonte.what: The regional government of Piedmont, an Italian region with ordinary statute created in 1948 and operating since 1970; seat in Turin.
regionepiemonte.money: The regional budget, which draws on its own taxes such as IRAP, regional surcharges and car tax.

reliance.money: The Ambani family’s money comes from Reliance Industries: oil refining and petrochemicals, retail, Jio telecoms, oil and gas, and media.

facts.t: Reliance Industries reported consolidated revenue of ₹10,71,174 crore (US$125.3 billion) for 2024-25, up 7.1%.
In January 2021 SEBI fined Reliance Industries Rs 25 crore and Mukesh Ambani Rs 15 crore for manipulating trading in Reliance Petroleum shares in November 2007.
In December 2023 the Securities Appellate Tribunal quashed SEBI’s order against Mukesh Ambani and two other entities in the Reliance Petroleum case.
Eversheds Sutherland reported $195,000 in 2025 fees from Reliance Industries for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act (fourth quarter as amended).

remai.money: Frank and Ellen Remai’s money comes from Frank Remai’s real estate business in Saskatoon, given through the Frank and Ellen Remai Foundation.

repsol.money: Repsol's money comes from producing oil and gas, refining and selling fuels, chemicals, and electricity.

facts.t: Repsol reported a net income of €1.899 billion for 2025, up 8%, and adjusted net income of €2.568 billion, 15% lower than in 2024.
Repsol, S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Repsol, S.A. reported $980,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Repsol a D grade for its climate policy engagement.

rgionbourgognefranchecomt.what: The regional council of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, the French region formed on 1 January 2016 from Burgundy and Franche-Comté, seated in Besançon.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.money: A EUR 1.922 billion budget in 2025, led by EUR 699 million of national VAT revenue assigned by the French state.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.arts: Its 2025 budget gives EUR 33.7 million to culture and heritage.

rgiongrandest.what: The regional council of Grand Est, the French region formed in 2016 from Alsace, Champagne-Ardenne and Lorraine, seated in Strasbourg.
rgiongrandest.money: Mostly national VAT shared out by the French state (53% of French regions' operating revenue in 2024); its planned 2026 budget is EUR 4.1 billion.

rgionsud.what: The regional council of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, the south-eastern French region also called Région Sud, seated in Marseille.
rgionsud.money: Mainly a share of national VAT assigned by the French state; councillors adopted a EUR 3.2 billion budget for 2024.
rgionsud.arts: The 2024 budget gave EUR 67 million to arts and culture.

right:griffin.money: Ken Griffin’s money comes from Citadel, his hedge fund, and Citadel Securities, a market-making firm.

facts.t: Citadel’s flagship Wellington fund finished 2024 up 15.1%; the firm had $66 billion in assets under management in December.
Ken Griffin gave $100,000,000 in the 2024 election cycle, fifth among top contributors, according to OpenSecrets data cited by CBS News.
Citadel declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025, with 2.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Citadel reported $650,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Citadel Securities’ PAC gave $28,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 47% to Republicans and 53% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

Ken Griffin gave $108,360,344 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to Senate Leadership Fund ($30,000,000), Congressional Leadership Fund ($17,000,000) and Keystone Renewal PAC ($16,000,000), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

right:koch.money: The Koch fortune comes from Koch Industries, a private conglomerate in oil refining, pipelines, chemicals, fertilisers, paper and other industries.

facts.t: Forbes lists Koch Industries’ annual revenue at $125 billion on its 2026 list of private companies.
AFP Action, the Koch network’s super PAC, spent roughly $138.5 million on independent expenditures in the 2024 cycle, according to OpenSecrets.
In 2000 Koch Industries agreed to pay a $30 million civil penalty over oil spills from its pipelines in several US states.
Koch Government Affairs, the lobbying arm of Koch Industries, reported $9,320,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

KOCHPAC, the PAC of Koch, Inc. (formerly Koch Industries), gave $1,663,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 98% to Republicans and 0% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

Charles Koch gave $10,000 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, all of it to KOCHPAC, the PAC of Koch, Inc., in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

riotinto.money: Rio Tinto’s money comes from mining, mainly iron ore, plus aluminium, copper and other minerals.

facts.t: Rio Tinto reported net earnings of US$11,552 million and underlying earnings of $10.87 billion for 2024.
InfluenceMap gives Rio Tinto a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Rio Tinto blasted 46,000-year-old rock shelters at Juukan Gorge in May 2020; its chief executive resigned that September.
Rio Tinto declared EU lobbying costs of €900,000 to €999,999 for 2025, with 2.35 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Rio Tinto Services reported $1,140,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in three quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Rio Tinto America’s PAC gave $14,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 82% to Republicans and 18% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

robertomarinho.money: The Marinho family’s money comes from Grupo Globo, Brazil’s largest media group, with television, newspapers and streaming.

facts.t: Globo’s net profit fell to R$1.45 billion in 2025, despite growth in revenue.
Roberto Marinho, then president of the group, wrote in 1984 that it had supported the 1964 “revolution”; in 2013 Globo said that support for the coup had been an error.

roche.money: Roche's money comes from pharmaceuticals and diagnostics; the Hoffmann and Oeri families, descendants of the founder, control it, and their own foundations (LUMA, the Emanuel Hoffmann Foundation, the Laurenz Foundation) draw on that fortune. The facts below are about the company.

facts.t: Roche reported 2025 group sales of CHF 61,516 million and IFRS net income of CHF 13,799 million.
In May 1999 F. Hoffmann-La Roche agreed to plead guilty and pay a $500 million criminal fine in the US for leading a worldwide conspiracy to fix prices and allocate market shares for vitamins.
F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd and its affiliates reported $410,000 of their own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; Genentech and Roche Diagnostics are not counted.

rockefellerbrothers.money: The Rockefeller money comes from John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil fortune; the Rockefeller Brothers Fund was founded in 1940 by John D. Rockefeller Jr.'s five sons and endowed by him in 1951.

rogers.money: The Rogers family’s money comes from Rogers Communications, the wireless, cable and media company it controls; the ties here are gifts in the company’s name.

rolex.what: A Geneva watchmaker founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis, owned since 1960 by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
rolex.money: Sales of Rolex and Tudor wristwatches by a company wholly owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private Swiss foundation.
rolex.arts: Its Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative, set up in 2002, pairs emerging artists with established ones and gives each protégé about $41,000.

rosneft.money: Rosneft’s money comes from oil and gas production, refining and sales; its largest shareholder is the Russian state holding company Rosneftegaz.

royalinn.money: Royal Inn (老爺會館) is one of the hotels of the Hotel Royal group (老爺酒店集團), so its money comes from running hotels in Taiwan.

sabanci.money: The Sabancı family’s money comes from Sabancı Holding, a Turkish group in banking (Akbank), energy, building materials, mobility and digital businesses.

sacklerfamily.money: The Sackler fortune came from Purdue Pharma, the maker of the opioid painkiller OxyContin.

sainsbury.money: The Sainsbury family's money, and that of its charitable trusts (Linbury, Monument, Gatsby, Glass-House and others), comes from J Sainsbury plc, the supermarket group the family founded.

facts.t: J Sainsbury plc reported retail sales (including VAT, excluding fuel) of £29,992m and underlying profit before tax of £718m for the 52 weeks to 28 February 2026.

saintgobain.money: Saint-Gobain's money comes from making and selling building materials: glass, insulation, plaster and construction chemicals.

facts.t: Compagnie de Saint-Gobain declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 3.85 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Saint-Gobain Corporation paid the outside firm Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies $80,000 for US federal lobbying in 2025 (four quarterly reports of $20,000).

samsung.money: Samsung’s money comes from the Samsung group’s businesses, above all Samsung Electronics’ chips, phones and displays, and from the Lee family that controls it.

facts.t: Samsung Electronics reported 2025 revenue of KRW 333.6 trillion and operating profit of KRW 43.6 trillion.
