Lee Jae-yong, convicted of bribery and embezzlement in January 2021 and paroled in August 2021 after 18 months in prison, received a presidential pardon in August 2022.

santander.money: Banco Santander's money comes from retail and commercial banking in Europe and the Americas; the Botín family's Fundación Botín, which runs Centro Botín, draws its budget from the dividends on its Santander shares.

Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 reports that Santander almost doubled its fossil debt commitments in 2025 compared with 2021, while diluting its 2030 emissions targets and exclusion policies.
Banco Santander, S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Santander Holdings USA reported $700,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

sasktel.what: A telecommunications Crown corporation owned by the Government of Saskatchewan, founded in 1908 and based in Regina.
sasktel.money: Phone, wireless and internet services, with almost C$1.4 billion of annual revenue and C$104.7 million net income for 2025-26.

sberbank.money: Sberbank’s money comes from banking: it is Russia’s largest bank and majority-owned by the Russian government.

schlumberger.money: The de Menil money comes from the Schlumberger family's oilfield services company, now SLB, founded by Conrad and Marcel Schlumberger; SLB also gives as a company.

scotiabank.money: Scotiabank’s money comes from banking in Canada and Latin America, wealth management and capital markets.

facts.t: Scotiabank reported net income of $7,758 million for fiscal 2025, against $7,892 million; adjusted net income was $9,510 million.

In August 2020 the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered The Bank of Nova Scotia to pay $127.4 million for spoofing, false statements, and compliance and supervision violations in precious metals futures.

seplat.money: Seplat’s money comes from oil and gas production in Nigeria, onshore and offshore.

facts.t: Seplat Energy’s revenue rose 144.2% to $2,726 million in 2025, reflecting a full year of offshore assets.

shell.money: Shell’s money comes from producing, processing and selling oil and gas, including liquefied natural gas.

facts.t: Shell posted adjusted earnings of $23.72 billion for 2024, against $28.25 billion a year earlier.
Shell declared EU lobbying costs of €4,500,000 to €4,999,999 for 2025, with 13 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Shell a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Shell agreed a £55 million settlement with the Bodo community in Nigeria over two oil spills in 2008.
Shell USA reported $6,030,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

shiseido.money: Shiseido’s money comes from cosmetics and skincare.

shyllon.money: Yemisi Shyllon gives his own money and collection, through his art foundation; the records do not say how the money was made.

siemens.money: Siemens' money comes from industrial automation, software, rail and building technology and, through Siemens Healthineers, medical technology.

sigridrausingtrust.what: A London grant-making trust for human rights, open societies and the environment, established in 1995 by Sigrid Rausing.

simpsongrierson.money: A New Zealand law firm; its money is its partners' fees from legal work.

skgroup.money: SK Group’s money comes from energy and refining, telecoms (SK Telecom) and memory chips (SK hynix), under the Chey family.

sobey.money: The Sobey family’s money comes from Empire Company, owner of the Sobeys grocery chain, through family foundations.

socgen.money: Société Générale's money comes from retail and investment banking in France and abroad, including BRD in Romania.

sococimcement.money: Sococim’s money comes from making cement in Senegal; it is owned by the French group Vicat.

south32.money: South32 is a Perth miner of aluminium, alumina, manganese, zinc, silver and other metals.

facts.t: South32 reported underlying revenue of US$7,610 million and underlying earnings of US$666 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

sparebankstiftelsendnb.money: Dividends on its stake of about 8.9% in DNB.

sparknz.money: Spark, formerly Telecom New Zealand, sells mobile, broadband and IT services; the Spark Foundation is its charity.

srp.what: A not-for-profit Arizona utility run by the Salt River Valley Water Users' Association, formed in 1903, and the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District.

standardbank.money: Standard Bank’s money comes from banking and insurance, in South Africa and across the rest of Africa.

facts.t: Standard Bank Group reported headline earnings of R44 503 million for 2024, up 4%.

statenskunstfond.what: Denmark's state arts foundation, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, administered by a Ministry of Culture agency.

stateoflowersaxony|Germany.what: The science and culture ministry of the German state of Lower Saxony in Hanover, led since 8 November 2022 by Minister Falko Mohrs.
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.money: The state budget of Lower Saxony.

steeltube.money: Steel & Tube, listed on the NZX, makes and distributes steel products in New Zealand.

stockland.money: Stockland is a Sydney property developer and owner of shopping centres, housing estates and logistics property.

suncor.money: Suncor’s money comes from Alberta oil sands mining and upgrading, refining and its Petro-Canada fuel stations.

suntory.money: Suntory’s money comes from beer, spirits (Beam Suntory, now Suntory Global Spirits) and soft drinks.

swarovski.money: Swarovski's money comes from cut crystal, jewellery and accessories, a family-owned business based in Wattens, Austria.

swedishartscouncil|Sweden.what: A Swedish government agency under the Ministry of Culture that distributes state cultural grants, based at Filmhuset in Stockholm.

swire.money: The Swire Charitable Trust's money comes from John Swire & Sons, the Swire family's trading group.

taishin.money: Taishin's money comes from banking and insurance, through Taishin Financial Holding.

tdbank.money: TD Bank Group’s money comes from retail and commercial banking in Canada and the eastern United States, wealth management, insurance and capital markets.

teck.money: Teck’s money comes from mining copper and zinc; it sold its steelmaking coal business in 2024.

telefonica.money: Telefónica's money comes from telecoms: mobile, broadband and pay-TV services in Spain, Germany, the UK and Latin America.

telstra.money: Telstra is Australia’s largest telecommunications company.

tepco.money: TEPCO’s money comes from generating and selling electricity in the Tokyo region; it operated the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.

todd.money: The Todd family's Todd Corporation, whose Todd Energy produces natural gas, oil and LPG from onshore fields in Taranaki.

torontoartscouncil|Canada.what: Toronto's city-wide public funding body for the arts, created in 1974; a charitable organization working under an arm's-length funding agreement with the City of Toronto.

totalenergies.money: TotalEnergies’ money comes mainly from producing, refining and selling oil and gas, including liquefied natural gas.

toyota.money: The ties name Toyota Tsusho, the Toyota group’s trading company, and Toyota-Fonden, a Danish foundation bearing the Toyota name.

tunisair.what: Tunisia's national airline, formed by the government in 1948 and based near Tunis-Carthage International Airport.

ubs.money: UBS’s money comes from wealth management, investment banking and asset management.

unicredit.money: UniCredit's money comes from banking in Italy, Germany (HypoVereinsbank), Austria (Bank Austria) and Central and Eastern Europe.

vale.money: Vale’s money comes from mining, mainly iron ore, and nickel and copper.

vancleef.what: A French jewellery house founded in Paris in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, owned by the luxury group Richemont since 1999.

vgc.what: The body that represents the Flemish authorities in the Brussels-Capital Region, created by the special law of 12 January 1989 and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
vgc.money: A dotation from the Flemish government's budget, EUR 30,588,000 in 2025, plus EUR 1,116,000 a year for community infrastructure.
vgc.arts: It runs more than 20 Dutch-language public libraries, including Muntpunt, and 22 community centres in Brussels.

vinci.money: Vinci's money comes from building and civil engineering (Vinci Construction) and from running motorways, airports and other concessions.

vitra.money: The Fehlbaum family's money comes from Vitra, the Swiss furniture company it owns, which makes and sells designer furniture.

vladimirpotanin.money: Vladimir Potanin’s money comes from metals, through Interros and his stake in Norilsk Nickel, which he heads.

facts.t: On 15 December 2022 the US State Department designated Potanin, one of Russia’s richest men, and the Treasury designated Rosbank, a bank he had acquired that year.

volkswagen.money: Volkswagen's money comes from making and selling cars and vans under brands including Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche, and from car finance; Porsche Holding Salzburg, its car importer and dealer, belongs to Volkswagen AG.

facts.t: The Volkswagen Group reported 2025 sales revenue of 321.9 billion euros and an operating result of 8.9 billion euros, 53% below 2024.

In the US diesel emissions case over defeat devices that cheated federal emissions tests, Volkswagen paid a $1.45 billion civil penalty under the Clean Air Act and funded a $2.7 billion mitigation trust; Audi AG and Porsche AG were among the defendants.
Volkswagen AG declared EU lobbying costs of €2,750,000 to €2,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Volkswagen Group of America reported $1,150,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Volkswagen a C grade for its climate policy engagement.

vriendenloterij.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterij.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterij.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vsbfonds.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht named after the Verenigde Spaarbank (VSB), formed in 1983 from 19th-century Nutsspaarbanken savings banks.
vsbfonds.money: Returns on capital held by Stichting VSB Vermogensfonds, built from the VSB shares the fund owned after the bank merged into Fortis in 1990.

vtb.money: VTB’s money comes from banking: it is Russia’s second-largest bank, controlled by the Russian state.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on VTB Bank, which it described as Russia’s second-largest financial institution, holding nearly 20 percent of banking assets in Russia.

walmart.what: A US retailer founded in 1962 by the brothers Sam and Bud Walton, running Walmart stores and Sam's Club, headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas.
walmart.money: Retail sales; total revenue was US$713.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

waltonfamily.money: The Walton family's money comes from Walmart, the retailer Sam Walton founded; the family's gifts go through the Walton Family Foundation and Alice Walton, the company's through Walmart Inc. and the Walmart Foundation.

facts.t: Walmart reported total revenues of $713,163 million for the fiscal year to January 2026.
In November 2022 state attorneys general announced a proposed $3.1 billion multistate settlement with Walmart over its role in the opioid epidemic.
Walmart reported $7,840,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

warholfdn.what: A New York nonprofit set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which also serves as the artist's estate.
warholfdn.money: An endowment built from Warhol's assets, plus income from licensing and selling his works.
warholfdn.arts: It has given more than US$300 million in cash grants to over 1,000 arts organisations in 49 states and abroad.

wellsfargo.money: Wells Fargo's money comes from consumer and commercial banking, lending and wealth management.

facts.t: Wells Fargo reported net income of $21,338 million for 2025.
In December 2022 the CFPB ordered Wells Fargo to pay more than $2 billion in consumer redress and a $1.7 billion penalty over the mismanagement of auto loans, mortgages and deposit accounts.
Wells Fargo reported $2,700,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

wesfarmers.money: Wesfarmers is a Perth conglomerate whose money comes mostly from retail (Bunnings, Kmart, Officeworks), with chemicals, energy and fertiliser plants beside it.

facts.t: Wesfarmers reported revenue of $45.7 billion and a statutory net profit after tax of $2,926 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Wesfarmers Limited disclosed $61,800 in political donations: $34,300 to Labor branches and $27,500 to Liberal and National branches.

wesfarmersarts.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmersarts.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmersarts.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.

westpac.money: Westpac is one of Australia’s four major banks.

facts.t: Westpac reported a net profit after tax of $6.9 billion for the year to 30 September 2025.

In 2020 the Federal Court ordered Westpac to pay a $1.3 billion penalty for breaches of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing law, including failing to report international funds transfer instructions.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Westpac Banking Corporation disclosed $193,049 in political donations: $94,811 to Labor branches and $98,238 to Liberal and National branches.

wexner.money: Les Wexner's money comes from L Brands (The Limited), the retail group behind Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works, since split into two companies.

facts.t: In August 2019 Wexner wrote to the Wexner Foundation community that his former friend and personal money manager Jeffrey Epstein had misappropriated 'vast sums of money from me and my family' more than ten years earlier.
In February 2026 Wexner testified about his relationship with Epstein in a closed-door deposition before the House Oversight Committee, at his home in Ohio.

wienerstdtische.what: An Austrian insurer founded in Vienna in 1824, the largest single company in the Vienna Insurance Group.
wienerstdtische.money: Insurance premiums, about EUR 3,196.2 million gross; the Wiener Städtische Versicherungsverein is the group's main shareholder.

wihurifoundation.money: The foundation was set up in 1942 by the industrialist Antti Wihuri and his wife Jenny Wihuri.

winnipegartscouncil|Canada.what: A not-for-profit charity that the City of Winnipeg charges with distributing its arts funding and managing its Public Art Policy.
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.money: City arts funding of C$4.65 million in 2025, plus C$258,570 for five city-designated museums.

wipro.money: Wipro's money comes from IT services; Azim Premji, its founder chairman, gives through the Azim Premji Foundation, and the Wipro Foundation is the company's own.

facts.t: Wipro's IT Services revenues for FY25 amounted to USD 10.51 billion, a year-on-year degrowth of 2.3%.

wolfson.what: A UK grant-making charity set up in 1955 by Isaac Wolfson, chairman of Great Universal Stores, with his wife and son Leonard; based in London.
wolfson.money: Its endowment, just under £1 billion in 2024, when it spent £44 million on charitable activities.

wrth.what: A family-owned German group selling fastening and assembly materials, founded by Adolf Würth in Künzelsau in 1945 and led by his son Reinhold Würth from 1954.
wrth.money: Sales through more than 400 companies in 80 countries, EUR 20.7 billion in 2025.
wrth.arts: Its Kunsthalle Würth reopened in October 2026 for its 25th anniversary.

wurth.money: The Würth family's money comes from the Würth Group, a maker and seller of assembly and fastening materials built up by Reinhold Würth.

facts.t: The Würth Group reported preliminary 2025 sales of EUR 20.7 billion and an operating result of EUR 940 million.

In May 2008 Reinhold Würth accepted a penalty order of 700 daily fines from the Heilbronn District Court in his tax affair, which the Heilbronner Stimme put at €3.5 million assuming net income of at least €1.8 million.
Adolf Würth GmbH & Co. KG declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 0.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

wynn.money: Wynn Resorts runs casino resorts in Las Vegas, Macau and Boston; its founder Steve Wynn resigned as chief executive in 2018.

facts.t: Wynn Resorts posted full-year 2025 revenue of $7.1 billion, flat on 2024.

In April 2019 the Massachusetts Gaming Commission fined Wynn Resorts $35 million after executives failed to disclose years of sexual misconduct allegations against founder Steve Wynn, and fined CEO Matthew Maddox $500,000.

Outside firms reported $460,000 in 2025 fees for US federal lobbying for Wynn Resorts and Wynn Resorts Development (Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck $190,000, Dentons $150,000, Empire Consulting Group $120,000); the company filed no in-house report.

yandex.money: Yandex’s money comes from internet services in Russia and nearby countries: search, ride hailing (Yandex Go), food delivery (Yandex Eda) and advertising.

yanshijie.money: Yan Shijie is a collector and entrepreneur; the sources read do not name the business his money comes from.

yarur.money: The Yarur family’s money comes from Banco de Crédito e Inversiones (BCI), the Chilean bank it controls.

facts.t: BCI reported net profit of 996,212 million Chilean pesos for 2025.

yokonagaeceschina.money: Yoko Nagae Ceschina’s money was the $190 million fortune she inherited from her husband, Count Renzo Ceschina.

zhenghao.money: Zheng Hao's money comes from hotels, among them the Onehome Art Hotel in the park the museum shares.

zinsou.money: The Zinsou family finances the foundation; its Circle of Major Patrons lists Lionel Zinsou, Marie-Cécile Zinsou’s father, and Marie-Christine Zinsou.
